ITQAN:v4p336/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p336/r5.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v4p336/r5.claim: Al-Raghib says the Qur'an's small size contains meaning so vast that human minds cannot enumerate it and worldly instruments cannot exhaust it.
ITQAN:v4p336/r5.anchor: وجعل من معجزة هذا الكتاب أنه مع قلة الحجم متضمن للمعنى الجم

QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r19.claim: Even if every tree became a pen, seas became ink, and all pages and writers were spent, God’s meanings and speech would not be exhausted.
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r19.anchor: مانفدت معاني ما لنا معك من الكلام

QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r20.claim: Human resources and speech run out, while what is with God remains; His eternal word has no end.
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r20.anchor: فما عندكم ينفذ وما عند الله باق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r8.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the two verses beginning “If all the trees on earth were pens” and continuing it were revealed in Medina.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r8.anchor: وروي عن عطاء أنه قال هي مكية سوى آيتين منها نزلتا بالمدينة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p346/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p346/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p346/r3.claim: Commentators say Jews first asked about the spirit, prompting 17:85; after migration they challenged the claim of limited knowledge against the Torah's scope and the Quran's description of wisdom as great good, and 31:27 was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p346/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: سألت اليهود رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الروح، فأنزل الله بمكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r1.claim: Three poetic examples illustrate Arabic counterfactuals introduced by “law,” a construction also used in the verse about trees as pens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r1.anchor: ولو أنها عصفورة لحسبتها ... مسومة تدعو عبيدا وأيما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r2.claim: With the majority’s nominative “and the sea,” the waw is most naturally circumstantial and “the sea” is the subject of “would supply it.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن الواو في قوله: والبحر، في قراءة من رفع، وهم الجمهور، واو الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the sea clause as coordinated with the preceding clause about trees and the conditional “if.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: عطفا على محل إن ومعمولها على ولو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says that coordination only works on al-Mubarrad’s disputed view that “anna” occupies a subject position after “law.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r4.anchor: وهذا لا يتم إلا على رأي المبرد، حيث زعم أن أن في موضع رفع على الفاعلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r5.claim: Some grammarians coordinate the sea with “anna,” but that would put a bare subject after “law,” ordinarily allowed only in poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r5.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: هو عطف على أن، لأنها في موضع رفع بالابتداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r6.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r6.claim: Abd Allah reads “and a sea” as an indefinite nominative; the waw can mark a circumstantial clause or coordinate it with earlier material.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: وبحر يمده، بالتنكير بالرفع، والواو للحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r7.claim: Most readers use “yمده” with yāʾ; Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas use feminine tāʾ, while other named readers use the form from “amadda.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يمده بالياء، من مد وابن مسعود، وابن عباس: بتاء التأنيث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r8.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r8.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad reads “the sea is its ink”; Ibn Atiyya calls “مداده” a verbal noun.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r9.claim: “Seven seas” signals abundance rather than a literal limit; the form “seas” is a paucity plural that matches the number’s form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p419/r9.anchor: لا يراد به الاقتصار على هذا العدد، بل جيء به للكثرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r1.claim: The omitted meaning is that if pens and all the sea’s ink wrote God’s words, they would run out before His words did.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r1.anchor: ما نفدت، والمعنى: ولو أن أشجار الأرض أقلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r2.claim: This image parallels the verse saying the sea would be ink for God’s words; the supply would be exhausted while His words remained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r2.anchor: كما قال: لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks how the circumstantial sea clause can lack a pronoun linking it to its subject and proposes “its sea,” referring to earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: زعمت أن قوله: والبحر يمده، حال في أحد وجهي الرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says an independent nominal clause introduced by a circumstantial waw needs no linking pronoun; it is unlike a circumstantial adverb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي جعله سؤالا وجوابا من واضح النحو الذي لا يجهله المبتدءون فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r5.claim: Reading “the sea” as “its sea” works only under the Kufan view that the definite article can replace a pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r5.anchor: وأما قوله: ويجوز، فلا يجوز إلا على رأي الكوفيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the singular “a tree” as distributing the image tree by tree until every individual tree becomes a pen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: لم قيل: من شجرة، على التوحيد دون اسم الجنس الذي هو شجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r7.claim: Arabic can use an indefinite singular after “of” to mean an entire plural class, as in verses about any sign, mercy, or creature.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r8.claim: Each tree has many branches that could each be cut into a pen, producing a quantity beyond reckoning except by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p420/r8.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام من المبالغة في تكثير الأقلام والمداد ما ينبغي أن يتأمل

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.claim: The preceding statement that all in heaven and earth belong to God might suggest a finite dominion; this verse counters that inference with wonders beyond limit in His power and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r1.anchor: وكان ذلك موهما لتناهي ملكه لانحصار ما في السموات وما في الأرض فيهما

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r2.claim: Here God's words mean His wonders: wonders come about by the word Be, so the name of the cause is applied to its effect; Arabic also calls a brave opponent one's death or medicine one's cure.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا فالكلمة مفسرة بالعجيبة ، ووجهها أن العجائب بقوله كن وكن كلمة

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r3.claim: Jesus is called a word because his existence without a father was wondrous, supporting the interpretation of God's words as wonders.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r3.anchor: الله تعالى سمى المسيح كلمة لأنه كان أمرا عجيبا وصنعا غريبا لوجوده من غير أب

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r4.speaker: اليهود
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r4.claim: One reported occasion is that Jews claimed the Torah had mentioned everything, leaving nothing unmentioned; the verse answers that the Torah is only a drop beside God's speech.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r4.anchor: الآية واردة في اليهود حيث قالوا الله ذكر كل شيء في التوراة ولم يبق شيء لم يذكره

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r5.speaker: واحد
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r5.claim: Another reported occasion concerns a man who challenged the Prophet by juxtaposing the claim that human knowledge is little with the claim that wisdom is great good; the verse says it is much for people but little relative to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r5.anchor: وقيل أيضا إنها نزلت في واحد قال للنبي عليه السلام إنك تقول

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r6.speaker: الكفار
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r6.claim: A further reported occasion is a response to disbelievers who said Muhammad's teachings would run out: God's speech does not run out.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r6.anchor: وقيل أيضا إنها نزلت ردا على الكفار حيث قالوا بأن ما يورده محمد سينفد

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r7.claim: The different reported occasions are disparate, showing the verse is general and can answer all of them; this general reading does not conflict with understanding the words as speech.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r7.anchor: ما ذكرتم من اختلاف الأقوال فيه يدل على جواز ما ذكرنا

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r8.claim: God's speech is wondrous and inimitable, and belongs among His limitless wonders; the created letters and arrangement are wondrous, while the words themselves are God's attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r8.anchor: كلام الله عجيب معجز لا يقدر أحد على الإتيان بمثله

RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r9.claim: Although the verse's revealed sequence differed from its written sequence, the Quran's written arrangement was commanded by God through the Messenger and is established by transmitted practice.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137/r9.anchor: واعلم أن الآية وإن كانت نازلة على ترتيب غير الذي هو مكتوب

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r1.claim: The singular tree with plural pens, rather than plural trees and singular pens, signals abundance: there would be pens equal in number to every tree.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r1.anchor: وحد الشجرة وجمع الأقلام ولم يقل ولو أن ما في الأرض من الأشجار أقلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r2.claim: The definite article in al-baḥr is generic and encompasses every sea; the seven seas added after it are hypothetical seas beyond those that exist.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r2.anchor: تعريف البحر باللام لاستغراق الجنس وكل بحر مداد

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r3.claim: Seven does not limit the number: it signifies abundance, even if a thousand seas were added.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r3.anchor: وقوله : { سبعة } ليس لانحصارها في سبعة ، وإنما الإشارة إلى المدد والكثرة ولو بألف بحر

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r4.claim: Seven became a customary number for encompassing many because space was divided into seven climes, time into seven days, and the planets were seven, to which astrologers assigned effects.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r4.anchor: هو أن ما هو معلوم عند كل أحد لحاجته إليه هو الزمان والمكان

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r5.claim: After ten, counting restarts at units, then hundreds build on tens and thousands on hundreds; three is the minimum complete form of beginning, middle, and end, leaving seven as the larger part of ten and a sign of abundance.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r5.anchor: أقل ما يلتئم منه أكثر المعدودات هو الثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r6.claim: The threefold counts of prayer-transition glorifications and ablution washings ease the duty by using the smaller first portion.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r6.anchor: فإن المعدودات في العبادات من التسبيحات في الانتقالات في الصلوات ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r7.claim: The saying that a believer eats with one intestine and a disbeliever with seven signifies little versus much eating, not the specific number seven; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r7.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( المؤمن يأكل في معى والكافر يأكل في سبعة أمعاء ) إشارة إلى قلة الأكل

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r8.claim: On the same interpretation, Hell's seven gates may signal multitude; Paradise's eight gates signal its added excellence and abundance, as it contains the good and more.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال إن لجهنم سبعة أبواب بهذا التفسير

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls the conjunction before eight the wāw of eight; Razi explains it as a fresh count because customary counting completes at seven.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r9.anchor: يقول الفراء إنها واو الثمانية وليس ذلك إلا للاستئناف

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r10.claim: No further supply is specified for the pens because the phrase already gives as many pens as existing trees, exceeding the trees; adding supplies for pens would make the sea and pens equivalent in meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r10.anchor: بينا أن المراد منه هو أن يكون بعدد كل شجرة موجودة أقلام فتكون الأقلام أكثر من الأشجار الموجودة

RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r11.claim: The sea is given additional supplies because writing consumes ink, while one pen can write many books.
RAZI-FULL:v25p137#2/r11.anchor: النقصان بالكتابة يلحق المداد أكثر فإنه هو النافد والقلم الواحد يمكن أن يكتب به كتب كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r1.claim: An unattributed poem describes the many orbits carrying stars, sun and moon, and says human past and future have no weight in God's domain.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r1.anchor: يا أيها الناس كم لله من فلك … تجري النجوم به والشمس والقمر هين على الله ماضينا وغابرنا

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: Research into bodies, minerals, plants and animals contains countless questions; a lifetime devoted to even a small part would end before reaching their depths, illustrating the inexhaustible divine words.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: البحث عن هذه الأقسام التي ذكرناها للمتحيزات مشتمل على ألوف ألوف من المسائل

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r3.claim: The vast variety of created things falls under the Quranic description Lord of the Worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r3.anchor: وهي بأسرها وأجمعها داخلة تحت قوله ﴿ رب العالمين ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r4.claim: Divine mercy means both freeing people from kinds of affliction and bringing good to those in need.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r4.anchor: الرحمة عبارة عن التخليص من أنواع الآفات وعن إيصال الخيرات إلى أصحاب الحاجات

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r5.claim: Understanding God's deliverance from harm requires knowing the many kinds of affliction, most of which only God can know; medical study offers only a glimpse through illnesses affecting each organ.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r5.anchor: أما التخليص عن أقسام الآفات فلا يمكن معرفته إلا بعد معرفة أقسام الآفات وهي كثيرة لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r6.claim: God's guidance of human reason toward food and medicines from minerals, plants and animals reveals another boundless dimension of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r6.anchor: كيف هدى عقول الخلق إلى معرفة أقسام الأغذية والأدوية من المعادن والنبات والحيوان

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r7.speaker: جالينوس
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r7.claim: Galen said he withheld from his book on the eye's benefits an account of God's wisdom in making the hollow optic nerves meet; after an angel in a dream rebuked him, he awoke and wrote about it. No grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r7.anchor: وقد حكى جالينوس أنه لما صنف كتابه في منافع أعضاء العين قال : بخلت على الناس بذكر حكمة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r8.speaker: جالينوس
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r8.claim: Galen said his thickened spleen resisted every treatment; after dreaming of an angel's instruction, he bled the vein between his little and ring fingers. No grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r8.anchor: وقال أيضا : إن طحالي قد غلظ فعالجته بكل ما عرفت فلم ينفع فرأيت في الهيكل كأن ملكا نزل من السماء

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r9.claim: Al-Razi says many early medical discoveries arose through analogous insights and inspirations, showing that God's mercy to people exceeds enumeration.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r9.anchor: واكثر علامات الطب في أوائلها تنتهي إلى أمثال هذه التنبيهات والإلهامات

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r10.claim: A human being is like a traveler in this world, moving toward the abode of the afterlife where lasting righteous deeds bring success.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r10.anchor: الإنسان كالمسافر في هذه الدنيا وسنوه كالفراسخ وشهوره كالأميال وأنفاسه كالخطوات

RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r11.claim: The wonders of earth and heavens witnessed along life's route should lead one to imagine the greater joy, bliss and happiness of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v1p18/r11.anchor: فلينظر أنه كيف يكون عجائب حال عالم الآخرة في الغبطة والبهجة والسعادة

STUDYQURAN:31:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r1.claim: The image conveys the inexhaustibility of God's creative speech, as in the command Be, through which creation comes into being.
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r1.anchor: This verse evokes the inexhaustibility of God’s creation through Divine Speech

STUDYQURAN:31:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r2.claim: In this context, seven more seas is figurative language for an immeasurable quantity, not a literal count.
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r2.anchor: seven more is not literal, but is meant to indicate an immeasurable quantity (IK, R)

STUDYQURAN:31:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r3.claim: Because God's possible creations are infinite, even innumerable pens and immeasurable seas of ink would be exhausted before His creative speech.
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r3.anchor: immeasurable seas of ink and innumerable pens would be exhausted before God’s creative speech would be exhausted

STUDYQURAN:31:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r4.claim: One account says the verse followed a dispute in Madinah: Jewish leaders asked whether the little knowledge mentioned in 17:85 meant theirs or the Muslims'; Muhammad answered both, and said God's knowledge dwarfed theirs despite the Torah's clarification.
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r4.anchor: Then God sent this verse in response to what they had asked (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:31:27/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r5.speaker: W
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r5.claim: Another account has the Prophet say their knowledge was little beside God's, though sufficient if practiced; Jews raised the apparent tension with wisdom as much good, and the verse was revealed in reply.
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r5.anchor: Then as a response, God revealed this verse (W)

STUDYQURAN:31:27/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r6.claim: Others say the verse may have answered disbelievers who claimed that Muhammad's revelations would soon be exhausted.
STUDYQURAN:31:27/r6.anchor: Others say that this verse may have been revealed in relation to a group of disbelievers

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r1.claim: The verse may answer Jews who questioned the Prophet, or Quraysh envoys asked about 17:85; human and Torah knowledge is only a drop beside God's.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r1.anchor: جواب لليهود حين سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو أمروا وفد قريش أن يسألوه عن قوله

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says polytheists claimed the Qur'an would soon run out, prompting this verse.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة : قال المشركون القرآن يوشك أن ينفد وينقطع فنزلت.

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r3.claim: Min shajarah qualifies the relative pronoun; the singular itemizes each individual tree.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r3.anchor: {من شجرة} حال من الموصول وهي ماله ساق وتوحيدها لما أن المراد تفصيل الأحاد

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r4.claim: Every individual tree would be entirely shaved down to make pens.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r4.anchor: يعني أن كل فرد من جنس الشجر بحيث لا يبقى منه شيء لو برى قلما

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r5.claim: Qalam originally means something cut from a hard object, then became the name for a writing tool.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r5.anchor: وأصل القلم القص من الشيء الصلب كالظفر وخص ذلك بما يكتب به

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r6.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r6.claim: Kashf al-Asrār derives qalam from cutting its tip and links the root to a land district and trimming nails.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r6.anchor: في "كشف الأسرار" : سمي قلما لأنه قط رأسه والإقليم القطعة من الأرض وتقليم الأظفار قطعها.

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r7.claim: Qaṭṭ cuts across, qadd lengthwise, and qaṭʿ separates a body by another body's penetration.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r7.anchor: والفرق بين القط والقد أن القط القطع عرضا والقد القطع طولا والقطع فصل الجسم بنفوذ جسم آخر فيه.

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r8.claim: The sea is the vast encompassing ocean and source of all connected or separate seas; its shore is unknown, its depth known only to God, and earthly seas are its inlets.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r8.anchor: البحر المحيط بسعته وهو البحر الأعظم الذي منه مادة جميع البحار المتصلة والمنقطعة وهو بحر لا يعرف له ساحل

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r9.claim: Bursevī says Iblīs's throne, floating jinn cities, coral trees, and countless known and unknown islands are in this ocean.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r9.anchor: وفي هذا البحر عرش إبليس لعنه الله وفيه مدائن تطفو على وجه الماء وأهلها من الجن في مقابلة الربع الخراب

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r10.claim: Yamudduhu means to add to or pour into the sea, like adding ink to an inkpot.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r10.anchor: أي : يزيده وينصب فيه من مد الدواة جعلها ذات مداد وزاده فيها

BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r11.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r11.claim: The cited other seas include China, Tibet, India, Sind, Persia, East, and West.
BURSEVI:v7p70#2/r11.anchor: نحو بحر الصين وبحر تبت كسكر على ما في "القاموس" وبحر الهند وبحر السند وبحر فارس

BURSEVI:v7p71/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r1.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
BURSEVI:v7p71/r1.claim: Asʾilat al-Ḥikam says God adorned the world with seven seas and seven regions; Bursevī tentatively lists seven rivers instead.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r1.anchor: قال في "أسئلة الحكم" : إن الله زين الدنيا بسبعة أبحر وسبعة أقاليم

BURSEVI:v7p71/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r2.claim: Bursevī tentatively identifies the seven as Euphrates, Tigris, Seyhan, Seyhun, Jeyhan, Jeyhun, and Nile, since Arabs call abundant water a sea.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد الأنهار السبعة من الفرات ودجلة

BURSEVI:v7p71/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p71/r3.claim: Al-Kāshifī understands seven more seas like it, with the number expressing abundance.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r3.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : {سبعة أبحر} (هفت درياى ديكر مانند او) انتهى فيكون ذكر العدد للتكثير

BURSEVI:v7p71/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r4.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p71/r4.claim: Al-Irshād says the seven seas augment the ocean because they adjoin mountains and springs, receiving major rivers before these flow to the ocean.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r4.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" إسناد المد إلى الأبحر السبعة دون البحر المحيط مع كونه أعظم منها وأطم

BURSEVI:v7p71/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r5.claim: Pens and ink would run out while writing, but God's words—the objects of His knowledge and wisdom—would not; 18:109 makes the same comparison.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r5.anchor: وبذلك المداد كلمات الله {ما نفدت كلمات الله} أي : ما فنيت متعلقات علمه وحكمته

BURSEVI:v7p71/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r6.claim: The small-number plural signals that the materials mentioned cannot encompass even a little of God's words.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r6.anchor: وإيثار جمع القلة في الكلمات للإيذان بأن ما ذكر لا يفي بالقليل منها فكيف بالكثير

BURSEVI:v7p71/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p71/r7.claim: Finite pens, seas, pages, and a writer's life cannot exhaust God's meanings: the finite cannot encompass the infinite and eternal.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r7.anchor: لأن هذه الأشياء وإن كثرت فهي متناهية ومعاني كلامه لا تتناهى لأنها قديمة والمحصور لا يفي بما لا حصر له

BURSEVI:v7p71/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r8.claim: The verse points to the Qur'an's pre-eternity, since unendingness characterizes the eternal.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r8.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة ظاهرة إلى قدم القرآن فإن عدم التناهي من خاصية القديم

BURSEVI:v7p71/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r9.claim: A statement says the Qur'an's wonders do not end and no one reaches the depth of its meanings and benefits.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r9.anchor: وجاء في حق القرآن "ولا تنقضي عجائبه" أي : لا ينتهي أحد إلى كنه معانيه العجيبة

BURSEVI:v7p71/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r10.claim: Divine wisdom and the sciences of the wise do not run out; they flow from wisdom's spring and God's inexhaustible treasuries.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r10.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة أيضا إلى أن كلمات الحكماء الإلهية وعلومهم لا تنقطع أبدا لأنها من عيون الحكمة

BURSEVI:v7p71/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r11.claim: Some knowers receive limitless knowledge in a lightning-like instant; Bursevī asks what their state is across a lifetime.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r11.anchor: ولبعض العارفين تجلي برقي يعطي في مقدار طرفة عين من العلوم ما لا نهاية له

BURSEVI:v7p71/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p71/r12.claim: God is invincible and nothing escapes His knowledge and wisdom, so His words cannot be exhausted.
BURSEVI:v7p71/r12.anchor: لا يعجزه شيء {حكيم} لا يخرج عن علمه وحكمته أمر فلا تنفد كلماته

BURSEVI:v7p71#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p71#3/r1.speaker: الشيخ العطار
BURSEVI:v7p71#3/r1.claim: ʿAṭṭār's poem says worldly sovereignty ends at death and counsels leaving transient rule to follow Ibrāhīm ibn Adham's ascetic example.
BURSEVI:v7p71#3/r1.anchor:
قال الشيخ العطار قدس سره :
ه ملكت اين وتوه ادشاهى كه باشير اجل بر مى نيايى

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r1.claim: If all earth’s trees became pens and the sea supplied ink, writing God’s words would exhaust the pens and ink while His words remained inexhaustible.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r2.claim: The pronoun in yamudduhu refers back to the sea.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r2.anchor: قال: لو بريت أقلاما والبحر مدادا، فكتب بتلك الأقلام منه

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r3.claim: The wording omits the act of writing: with the pens and ink writing God’s speech, the pens would break and the ink run out, but His words would not.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r3.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام محذوف استغنى بدلالة الظاهر عليه منه، وهو يكتب كلام الله بتلك الأقلام، وبذلك المداد

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that if the trees became pens and the seas ink, God’s decrees would exhaust the waters and break the pens.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r4.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، قال: سألت الحسن عن هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r5.speaker: عمرو
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r5.claim: A report from ʿAmr pictures the earth’s trees shaved into pens and the sea, even when extended by seven seas, as ink for writing God’s words.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r5.anchor: قال: لو بريت أقلاما والبحر مدادا، فكتب بتلك الأقلام منه

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r6.claim: Qatāda says the polytheists thought this speech would soon run out; the verse answers that God’s wonders, wisdom, creation, and knowledge are inexhaustible.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jewish scholars in Medina challenged the claim that their knowledge was little, citing the Torah; the Prophet said it was little beside God’s knowledge, and this verse was revealed in response.
TAB-FULL:v18p571#3/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، أن أحبار يهود قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة: يا محمد أرأيت قوله

TAB-FULL:v18p574/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r1.claim: ʿIkrima reports that the People of the Book challenged the statement that their knowledge was little by citing Torah and wisdom; 31:27 answered that knowledge useful for salvation is much for them but little beside God’s knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " سأل أهل الكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح، فأنزل الله {ويسألونك عن الروح

TAB-FULL:v18p574/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r2.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ b. Yasār recounts the Jews’ question in Medina; the Prophet said the charge of little knowledge concerned both them and his people, and God’s knowledge far exceeds the Torah.
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار، قال: " لما نزلت بمكة {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} [الإسراء: 85] يعني اليهود؛ فلما هاجر رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v18p574/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r3.claim: Medina and Kufa reciters read al-baḥru nominative as a new subject; Basra reciters read it accusative, coordinated with mā. Al-Ṭabarī accepts both.
TAB-FULL:v18p574/r3.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة: والبحر رفعا على الابتداء، وقرأته قراء البصرة نصبا، عطفا به على «ما» في قوله

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r6.claim: Min shajaratin explains the preceding relative expression; the singular collective tree, in the conditional construction, means every tree on earth.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r6.anchor: من شجرة } بيان للموصول والشجرة واحد الشجر

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r7.claim: Al-baḥr means the sea in general; seven seas means seven additional equivalents, with seven denoting abundance rather than an exact count.

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r8.claim: The number seven is used for abundance rather than to specify exactly seven added seas.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالسبعة التكثير دون خصوص هذا العدد

TABATABAI:31:26-27/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r9.claim: A word is an expression indicating meaning; in divine usage God's words can designate existents brought forth by his command and Jesus as God's word.
TABATABAI:31:26-27/r9.anchor: والكلمة هي اللفظ الدال على معنى،

TABATABAI:31:27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:27/r1.claim: If every tree became a pen and the sea plus seven equivalents became ink for God's words, the ink would run out first because his words are limitless.
TABATABAI:31:27/r1.anchor: فالمعنى ولو جعل أشجار الأرض أقلاما وأخذ البحر وأضيف إليه سبعة أمثاله

TABATABAI:31:27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:27/r2.claim: The passage is elliptical; the closing attributes explain that no one can overpower God and that in his wisdom he does not delegate governance.
TABATABAI:31:27/r2.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الكلام إيجازا بالحذف

TABATABAI:31:27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:27/r3.claim: God is unassailable and wise, so writing cannot exhaust what comes from him and he does not entrust governance to another.
TABATABAI:31:27/r3.anchor: حكيم لا يفوض التدبير إلى غيره

TABATABAI:31:27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:27/r4.claim: Following the proof of God's exclusive governance, this verse illustrates the vast reach of his creative and governing commands.
TABATABAI:31:27/r4.anchor: والآية متصلة بما قبلها من حيث دلالته على كون تدبير الخلق له سبحانه لا لغيره

TABRISI:31:27/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
TABRISI:31:27/r1.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read “the sea” in the accusative; the other readers read it in the nominative.
TABRISI:31:27/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب والبحر بالنصب والباقون بالرفع

TABRISI:31:27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
TABRISI:31:27/r2.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad reads “and the sea, its ink.”
TABRISI:31:27/r2.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد ع والبحر مداده

TABRISI:31:27/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وطلحة بن مصرف
TABRISI:31:27/r3.claim: Ibn Masud and Talha ibn Musarrif read “and a sea replenishes it.”
TABRISI:31:27/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود وبحر يمده وهي قراءة طلحة بن مصرف

TABRISI:31:27/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r4.speaker: الحسن والأعرج
TABRISI:31:27/r4.claim: Hasan and al-Aʿraj read “and the sea replenishes it” with a ḍamma on the yāʾ.
TABRISI:31:27/r4.anchor: الحسن والأعرج والبحر يمده بضم الياء

TABRISI:31:27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:31:27/r5.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes supplying people with wealth or men from adding another well when a cistern runs low.
TABRISI:31:27/r5.anchor: قال أبو زيد: أمددت القوم بمال ورجال إمدادا وقل ماء ركيتنا فمددتها

TABRISI:31:27/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:31:27/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda says the wording is abbreviated: if God's words were written with these pens and the sea, they would not be exhausted.
TABRISI:31:27/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: وها هنا اختصارا سبيله لو كتبت كلمات الله بهذه الأقلام والبحر

TABRISI:31:27/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:31:27/r7.claim: Abu Ali says the intended scope is what lies within possibility, apart from what has already come into existence.
TABRISI:31:27/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: والمراد بذلك والله أعلم ما في المقدور دون ما خرج منه إلى الوجود

TABRISI:31:27/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:31:27/r8.claim: Qatada says the pens would break and the seas' water run out before God's wonders, wisdom, creation, and knowledge did.
TABRISI:31:27/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: يقول لو كان شجر الأرض أقلاما ومع البحر سبعة أبحر مدادا إذا لانكسرت الأقلام

TABRISI:31:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27/r9.claim: On the accusative reading, “the sea” coordinates with the noun of “anna”; “it” in the verb refers back to the sea.
TABRISI:31:27/r9.anchor: فلأنه معطوف على اسم أن وهو ما في الأرض فما اسم أن وأقلام خبرها

TABRISI:31:27/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r10.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:31:27/r10.claim: On the nominative reading, one analysis begins a new clause: “and the sea is in this state,” as Sibawayh explains.
TABRISI:31:27/r10.anchor: ومن رفع استأنف كأنه قال: والبحر هذه حاله فيما قاله سيبويه:

TABRISI:31:27/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27/r11.claim: The author prefers accusative coordination with “anna,” eliding “ink” as the predicate; the following phrase is circumstantial.
TABRISI:31:27/r11.anchor: وأقول إذا عطفت البحر على اسم أن فنصبته فالأولى أن يكون خبره محذوفا

TABRISI:31:27/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27/r12.claim: The clause that seven seas replenish it can be circumstantial, with the omitted predicate “ink” supplied by context.
TABRISI:31:27/r12.anchor: ويمده سبعة أبحر يكون جملة منصوبة الموضع على الحال وحذف الخبر الذي هو مدادا

TABRISI:31:27/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27/r13.claim: If what is within God's power were written, the writing materials would run out before the realm of possibility was exhausted.
TABRISI:31:27/r13.anchor: وإذا نصبت البحر أو رفعته فالمعنى لو كتب ما في مقدور الله لنفد ذلك قبل نفاد المقدور

TABRISI:31:27/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27/r14.claim: The omitted wording has a parallel in the account of the Queen of Sheba receiving Solomon's letter and then speaking to her chiefs.
TABRISI:31:27/r14.anchor: كقوله اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم

TABRISI:31:27/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r15.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:31:27/r15.claim: Ibn Jinni rejects coordinating “a sea” with “pens,” since the sea and its water belong with ink, not with trees and pens.
TABRISI:31:27/r15.anchor: قال ابن جني: لا يجوز أن يكون وبحر معطوفا على أقلام لأن البحر وما فيه من الماء

TABRISI:31:27/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27/r16.claim: Nominative “the sea” may also coordinate with the syntactic position of “anna” and its noun, as in the raised “His Messenger” in 9:3.
TABRISI:31:27/r16.anchor: فأما رفع البحر فإن شئت كان معطوفا على موضع أن واسمها كما عطف عليه في قوله

TABRISI:31:27-30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r3.claim: Even if every earthly tree became pens and seven additional seas supplied ink, the pens and water would run out before God's words.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r3.anchor: أي لو كان شجر الأرض أقلاما وكان البحر مدادا ويمده سبعة أبحر مثله

TABRISI:31:27-30/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r4.claim: The author takes God's words as His possibilities and known things: because they are limitless, the words expressing them are limitless too.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r4.anchor: والأولى أن يكون عبارة عن مقدوراته ومعلوماته لأنها إذا كانت لا تتناهى فكذلك الكلمات

TABRISI:31:27-30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r5.claim: The author says his interpretation of God's words was discussed in Surat al-Kahf.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r5.anchor: وقد ذكرنا تفسير كلمات الله في سورة الكهف

TABRISI:31:27-30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r6.claim: God is mighty in His power over all things and wise in doing what accords with wisdom.

TABRISI:31:27-30/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r16.claim: Reading the verb with ḍamma on the yāʾ compares it to supplying an army with reinforcements.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r16.anchor: ومن قرأ يمده بضم الياء فإنه تشبيه بإمداد الجيش

TABRISI:31:27-30/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:27-30/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:27-30/r17.claim: The author rejects taking Jaʿfar's “sea is its ink” as the sea adding water to the writing ink, since seawater is not that ink.
TABRISI:31:27-30/r17.anchor: وليس يقوى أن يكون قراءة جعفر بن محمد ع والبحر مداده أي زائد فيه

THALABI:v7p321#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r1.speaker: قال المفسرون
THALABI:v7p321#2/r1.claim: Jewish scholars challenged how Torah could contain all knowledge when Quran calls knowledge little yet wisdom a great good; the report says this verse answered them.
THALABI:v7p321#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح فأنزل الله بمكة: ويسئلونك عن الروح الآية

THALABI:v7p321#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p321#2/r2.claim: Aqlām are pens made by trimming or sharpening branches.

THALABI:v7p321#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
THALABI:v7p321#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu ʿAmr, and Yaʿqub read al-baḥr accusative; others use nominative, supported by Ibn Masʿud's reading and a replenishing sea.
THALABI:v7p321#2/r3.anchor: والبحر بالنصب ابن أبي إسحاق وأبو عمرو ويعقوب. غيرهم بالرفع، وحجتهم: قراءة عبد الله وبحر يمده

THALABI:v7p321#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p321#2/r4.claim: The verse omits an implied clause: if pens and seven replenishing seas wrote God's words, they would not run out.
THALABI:v7p321#2/r4.anchor: وفي هذه الآية اختصار تقديرها: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر يكتب بها كلام الله ما نفدت كلمات الله

THALABI:v7p321#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p321#2/r5.claim: The verse entails that God's speech is uncreated because it has no end, including in its meaning.
THALABI:v7p321#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية تقتضي أن كلامه غير مخلوق لأنه لا نهاية له ولما يتعلق به من معناه فهو غير مخلوق

THALABI:v7p321#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r6.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
THALABI:v7p321#2/r6.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar considers the verse Medinan, revealed after the Hijra.
THALABI:v7p321#2/r6.anchor: هذه الآية على قول عطاء بن يسار: مدنية، قال: نزلت بعد الهجرة كما حكينا

THALABI:v7p321#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p321#2/r7.speaker: غيره
THALABI:v7p321#2/r7.claim: Other authorities call it Meccan, saying Jews instructed Quraysh to ask while Muhammad was still in Mecca.
THALABI:v7p321#2/r7.anchor: وعلى قول غيره: مكية، قالوا: إنما أمر اليهود وفد قريش أن يسألوا رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r1.claim: The word البحر is read in the accusative, coordinated with ما, or in the nominative as the start of a new sentence describing the sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r1.anchor: قرئ رفعا ونصبا، فمن نصبه عطفه على ما، ومن رفع استأنف كأنه قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r2.claim: The sea is supplied with, and increased by, seven further seas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r2.anchor: {يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر} أي: ينصب فيه ويزيده سبعة أبحر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r3.claim: God's words do not run out, and neither does His knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r3.anchor: {ما نفدت كلمات الله} ولا نفد علمه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r4.claim: Al-Suddi imagines all earthly trees made into pens and the sea plus seven seas as ink; the ink would run out before God's knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r4.anchor: قال السدي: لو كان ما في الأرض من شجر فبريت أقلاما، وكان البحر مدادا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says God's dictation would continue until the sea ran dry and the pens broke.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: لو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام، لأملى الله من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r6.claim: Muqatil says the pens and seas would be exhausted by writing, while God's knowledge would remain inexhaustible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول لو أن كل شجرة على وجه الأرض بريت أقلاما، وكانت البحور مدادا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r7.claim: Exegetes take God's words as His knowledge: since what He knows has no limit, the words expressing it likewise have no limit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r7.anchor: فالمفسرون قالوا في كلمات الله: إنها علم الله، والمعنى: الكلمات التي هي عبارات عن معلوم الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r8.claim: Abu Ali says the comparison concerns what is within God's power, rather than what has already passed from possibility into existence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: والمراد بذلك -والله أعلم- ما في المقدور دون بما خرج منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r9.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r9.claim: Qatada reports that polytheists said the Quran would soon run out; the verse answers that pens and seas would fail before God's words, judgment, creation, or knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: إن المشركين قالوا في القرآن: يوشك أن ينفد، يوشك أن ينقطع، فنزلت هذه الآية.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda calls the wording concise, with an implied clause: if one wrote with these pens and seas, God's speech would not run out.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r10.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: هذا مختصر، تقديره: فكتب هذه الأقلام والبحور ما نفد كلام الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r11.claim: The implied writing of all that is within God's power would exhaust its medium first; clauses like this can be omitted when context supplies them, as in the cited command to carry a letter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p121#3/r11.anchor: والمعنى (¬2): فكتب ما في مقدور الله لمنفد ذلك قبل أن ينفد المقدور

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r1.claim: The polytheists claimed the Qur’an’s speech would run out; God answers that His words are inexhaustible.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r1.anchor: وذلك أن المشركين قالوا في القرآن: هذا كلام سينفذ وينقطع، فأعلم الله سبحانه أن كلامه لا ينفد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r2.claim: The sea is increased by more water, and God’s words are then written with it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r2.anchor: أي: يزيد فيه، ثم كتبت به كلمات الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r3.claim: Even with every tree as pens and the seas as ink, God’s words would not be exhausted.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:27-31/r3.anchor: ثم كتبت به كلمات الله { ما نفدت }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r2.claim: The hypothetical has trees as pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, as ink for writing God's knowledge of what He created.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r2.anchor: ليكتب بها علم الله، علمه بما خلق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r3.claim: Some read al-baḥr in the accusative, understood as ولو أن البحر, coordinated with the preceding hypothetical.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r3.anchor: {والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر} [لقمان: 27] وبعضهم يقرأها بالنصب: والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر، أي: ولو أن البحر، تبع للكلام الأول

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r4.claim: The pens would break, the sea water run out, and the writer die, while God's words—His knowledge of what He created—would not run out.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r4.anchor: يعني: لانكسرت الأقلام، ونفد ماء البحر، ولمات الكتاب وما نفدت كلمات الله، علمه بما خلق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī explains God's words as God's knowledge and wonders.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: {ما نفدت كلمات الله} [لقمان: 27] ، يعني: علم الله وعجائبه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAmr reports that beneath the sea are alternating seas of fire and water, counting seven seas of each; Yaḥyā also gives a similar report through Saʿīd.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679#2/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: إن تحت بحركم هذا بحرا من نار

ELMALILI:31:20-30/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:20-30/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:20-30/r1.claim: For the image of trees as pens and the sea as ink, Elmalılı refers readers to 18:109.
ELMALILI:31:20-30/r1.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’te قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ [18/109] bak.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r5.claim: Verse 27 summarizes the richness and boundlessness of God’s knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r5.anchor: 27. âyette Allah’ın bilgisinin zenginliği ve sınırsızlığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.claim: The exclusive-praise claim rests on three premises: God’s absolute freedom to govern, knowledge beyond human comprehension, and power to create, sustain, or end all things with ease.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.anchor: 25. âyetteki “Bütün övgüler Allah’a mahsustur” hükmü, 27-29. âyetlerde şu üç öncüle dayandırılmıştır

BAQILLANI:v1p111/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r1.claim: Even the greatest poets fall short of Quranic composition; the author promises a separate comparison to make its distinction and inimitability clear.
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r1.anchor: وقد وقف على من هو أجل منه وأعظم قدرا في هذه الصنعة وأكبر في الطبقة كامرئ القيس وزهير

BAQILLANI:v1p111/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r2.claim: Poetic badiʿ cannot explain Quranic inimitability because such techniques can be learned, practiced, and deliberately assembled, whereas Quranic composition has no model and cannot arise by chance.
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r2.anchor: وذلك أن هذا الفن ليس فيه ما يخرق العادة ويخرج عن العرف

BAQILLANI:v1p111/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r3.claim: An individual may train himself to make all speech metrical or rhymed, and writers can collect rhetorical ornaments and apply them as they compose.
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r3.anchor: فرب إنسان يتعود أن ينظم جميع كلامه شعرا وآخر يتعود أن يكون جميع خطابه سجعا

BAQILLANI:v1p111/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r4.claim: Exceptional lines and striking meanings occur only occasionally in human poetry, letters, and sermons; if every line were exceptional, the extraordinary gap between human and Quranic composition would not be apparent.
BAQILLANI:v1p111/r4.anchor: ولو كان كل شعره نادرا ومثلا سائرا ومعنى بديعا ولفظا رشيقا وكل كلامه مملوءا من رونقه

BURHAN:v4p23/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p23/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p23/r5.claim: The wording أبحر rather than بحور suits the small-number plural and the verse’s arrangement.
BURHAN:v4p23/r5.anchor: ومن هذا قوله سبحانه ﴿ سبعة أبحر ﴾ 5 فاتى بجمع القلة ولم يقل بحور

BURHAN:v3p184/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p184/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p184/r3.claim: One reconstruction supplies ‘the pens and seas would be exhausted’ before the stated denial that God’s words would not be exhausted; another treats the denial itself as the apodosis, intensifying the assertion of inexhaustibility.
BURHAN:v3p184/r3.anchor: والتقدير لنفدت هذه الاشياء وما نفدت كلمات الله ويحتمل أن يكون ما نفدت هو الجواب مبالغة في نفي النفاد

BURHAN:v3p53/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p53/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p53/r2.claim: A second report assigns the revelation instead to the verse comparing all earthly trees to pens and the seas to ink.
BURHAN:v3p53/r2.anchor: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

BURHAN:v3p53/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p53/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p53/r3.claim: The commentators say the point is that God’s words are innumerable; the verse makes this comprehensible by comparing them with finite quantities, the greatest abundance people know.
BURHAN:v3p53/r3.anchor: والغرض من ذلك الإعلام بكثرة كلماته وهي في نفسها غير متناهية وإنما قرب الأمر على أفهام البشر

BURHAN:v3p53/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p53/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
BURHAN:v3p53/r4.claim: Some careful scholars say the verse asserts that God’s words would not run out, without asserting that even the imagined pens and seas could exhaust them; the source compares this with al-Khiḍr’s bird-and-sea analogy for divine knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p53/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين إن ما تضمنت الآية أن كلمات الله تعالى لم تكن لتنفد ولم تقتض الآية أنها تنفد

BURHAN:v3p27/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r3.claim: Repeated stories with varied wording do not become awkward or tiresome, unlike human speech.
BURHAN:v3p27/r3.anchor: فيها مع سائر الألفاظ لم يوقع في اللفظ هجنة ولا أحدث مللا

BURHAN:v3p27/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r4.claim: Addition, omission, and rearrangement keep repeated accounts from having identical wording and sounding merely repeated.
BURHAN:v3p27/r4.anchor: ومنها أنه ألبسها زيادة ونقصانا وتقديما وتأخيرا ليخرج بذلك الكلام أن تكون ألفاظه واحدة بأعيانها

BURHAN:v3p27/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r5.claim: Distributing a story's meanings across changing repetitions draws eloquent listeners through their love of novelty, giving each version a fresh share of pleasure.
BURHAN:v3p27/r5.anchor: ومنها أن المعاني التي اشتملت عليها القصة الواحدة

BURHAN:v3p27/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r6.claim: The varied compositions expressing related story meanings amazed the Prophet's contemporaries and point to God's inexhaustible speech, beyond any finite number of words.
BURHAN:v3p27/r6.anchor: فعرفهم الله سبحانه أن الأمر بما يتعجبون منه مردود إلى قدرة من لا يلحقه نهاية

BURHAN:v4p365/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p365/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p365/r1.claim: The verse's non-exhaustion holds even under the impossible supposition of every earthly tree as pens and seven seas as ink; the passage tests how لو relates a condition to its consequence.
BURHAN:v4p365/r1.anchor: فعدم النفاد في الآية الكريمة واقع على تقدير كون ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

BURHAN:v4p365/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p365/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p365/r3.claim: The praise of Suhayb—if he did not fear God, he would not disobey—presupposes his non-disobedience; denying that would contradict the praise's context.
BURHAN:v4p365/r3.anchor: نعم العبد صهيب لو لم يخف الله لم يعصه فنفي العصيان ثابت

BURHAN:v4p365/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p365/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p365/r4.claim: One account takes such لو clauses as linking the condition and result without implying that the result is otherwise impossible: non-exhaustion and Suhayb's obedience hold even more under the opposite condition.
BURHAN:v4p365/r4.anchor: دعوى أنها في مثل هذه المواضع أعنى الثابت فيها الثاني دائما إنما جاءت لمجرد الدلالة على ارتباط الثاني بالأول

BURHAN:v4p365/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p365/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p365/r5.claim: The author concludes لو makes its condition impossible and links it to the result, but does not establish whether that result is independently true; commonly neither condition nor result occurs.
BURHAN:v4p365/r5.anchor: والتحقيق أنها تفيد امتناع الشرط كما سبق من الآيات الشريفة وتحصل أنها تدل على أمرين

BURHAN:v4p367/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p367/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p367/r1.claim: An objection says that if لو made the consequent impossible whenever its condition is absent, the two statements about God knowing good and their turning away would conflict, since not turning away seems good.
BURHAN:v4p367/r1.anchor: فلو أفادت لو انتفاء الشيء لانتفاء غيره لزم التناقض

BURHAN:v4p367/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p367/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p367/r3.claim: One account of counterfactual لو says the consequent would follow from the condition if it occurred; its failure here concerns that causal scenario and does not rule out the consequent for another reason.
BURHAN:v4p367/r3.anchor: إن ما كان جوابا لها كان يقع لوقوع الأول فلما امتنع الأول

BURHAN:v4p367/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p367/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p367/r4.claim: A third analysis treats the answer to لو as omitted: if the trees became pens and the sea ink, those materials would be exhausted, while God's words would not be.
BURHAN:v4p367/r4.anchor: إن تحمل لو فيما جاء من ذلك على أنها محذوفة الجواب

BURHAN:v4p367/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p367/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p367/r5.claim: Alternatively, ما نفدت is the answer itself, or is preceded by an omitted conjunction, intensifying the denial that God's words could ever run out.
BURHAN:v4p367/r5.anchor: مستأنف أو على حذف حرف العطف أي وما نفدت

BURHAN:v4p369/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p369/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p369/r1.claim: The Kufans parse the noun after لو as the subject of an omitted verb, estimated as “if it were established that…,” which they consider more analogical because it preserves restriction.
BURHAN:v4p369/r1.anchor: وقال الكوفيون فاعل بفعل مقدر تقديره ولو ثبت أنهم

BURHAN:v4p369/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p369/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p369/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari requires the predicate of إن after لو to be verbal, so it can substitute for an omitted verb.
BURHAN:v4p369/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري يجب كون خبر إن الواقعة بعد لو فعلا

BURHAN:v4p369/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p369/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BURHAN:v4p369/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan calls al-Zamakhshari's rule a serious error: the verse has a nominal predicate, and Ibn al-Hajib and others likewise reject the rule, limiting it to derived predicates.
BURHAN:v4p369/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حيان هو وهم وخطأ فاحش قال الله تبارك وتعالى

BURHAN:v4p369/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p369/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p369/r4.claim: Some defend al-Zamakhshari by saying the coordinated clause “the sea replenishes it” can be mistaken for the predicate of the preceding clause because of the coordination.
BURHAN:v4p369/r4.anchor: وأيد بعضهم كلام الزمخشري بأنه إنما جاء من حيث إن قوله

BURHAN:v4p372/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p372/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p372/r1.claim: The answer to لو may be omitted when understood or for emphasis; in this verse it may mean the pens and seas would be exhausted, but God's words would not.
BURHAN:v4p372/r1.anchor: فيحتمل إن يكون جواب لو محذوفا والتقدير لنفدت هذه الأشياء

BURHAN:v4p372/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p372/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p372/r2.claim: Alternatively, ما نفدت is itself the answer: if God's words do not run out under the immense hypothetical abundance of writing materials, they certainly do not run out without it.
BURHAN:v4p372/r2.anchor: هو الجواب مبالغة في نفي النفاد

BURHAN:v3p204/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p204/r1.speaker: أبو الفتح
BURHAN:v3p204/r1.claim: Abu al-Fath supplies an omitted continuation: the pens and seas would write God's words, yet they would not be exhausted.
BURHAN:v3p204/r1.anchor: أي يكتب بذلك كلمات الله ما نفدت قاله أبو الفتح

BURHAN:v4p117/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p117/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p117/r5.claim: When the counted word is another kind of plural, the numeral is annexed to a broken plural of paucity to match the numeral's sense of small quantity; the verse says “seven seas.”
BURHAN:v4p117/r5.anchor: ثلاثة افلس واربعة اعبد قال تعالى

BURHAN:v4p364/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p364/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p364/r1.claim: The source presents four configurations of لو with its condition and answer: affirmative condition and answer, negation of both, negated condition with affirmative answer, and affirmative condition with negated answer.
BURHAN:v4p364/r1.anchor: وذكروا إن لها مع شرطها وجوابها أربعة أحوال

BURHAN:v4p364/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p364/r2.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p364/r2.claim: The author says Sibawayhi's account works throughout: the verse means the words would not be exhausted under the immense supposition, without implying that they would run out if the supposition were absent.
BURHAN:v4p364/r2.anchor: واعلم إن تفسير سيبويه لها مطرد في جميع مواردها

BURHAN:v4p364/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p364/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p364/r3.claim: For this verse, the counterfactual's implication is only that the words would not run out if trees and seas served as writing materials; it does not assert exhaustion in their absence.
BURHAN:v4p364/r3.anchor: ولا يلزم إلا يقع عدم نفاذ الكلمات إذا لم يجعل الشجر أقلاما

BURHAN:v4p364/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p364/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p364/r5.claim: The usual slogan “impossibility of one due to impossibility of the other” fails wherever evidence establishes the consequent absolutely; if the words do not run out amid abundant materials, they surely do not run out with fewer or none.
BURHAN:v4p364/r5.anchor: وأما تفسير من فسرها بأنها حرف امتناع لامتناع وذكر لها هذه الأحوال الأربعة فلا يطرد

BURHAN:v4p368/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p368/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p368/r1.claim: An objection says a conditional إن must be followed by a verb, whereas إن and its complement here are nominal; if لو functions like إن, it should not precede this construction.
BURHAN:v4p368/r1.anchor: فإن إن الشرطية لا يليها إلا الفعل

BURHAN:v4p368/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p368/r2.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p368/r2.claim: Al-Saffar replies that إن can be followed by a noun in surface form, so this is even more acceptable after لو, which may take such a phrase even outside its conditional use.
BURHAN:v4p368/r2.anchor: أجاب الصفار بأنه قد يلي إن الاسم في اللفظ

BURHAN:v4p368/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p368/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p368/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says لو links two verbal clauses as condition and result but is not intrinsically conditional; the conditional sense arises because the second proposition is impossible when the first is absent, and the answer takes a lām marker.
BURHAN:v4p368/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري فيما أفرده على سورة الحجرات لو تدخل على جملتين فعليتين

BURHAN:v3p398/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p398/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p398/r1.claim: The sea-as-ink comparison does not mean God's words end after the sea is spent: the sea would run out, but the words never run out, before or after it.
BURHAN:v3p398/r1.anchor: ليس المراد أن كلمات الله تنفذ بعد نفاذ البحر بل لا تنفذ أبدا

BURHAN:v3p398/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p398/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
BURHAN:v3p398/r8.claim: Al-Asma'i says he recited Jarir's line with “before”; Khalaf al-Ahmar corrected it to “less than,” a poetic wording variant used as evidence in the discussion.
BURHAN:v3p398/r8.anchor: قال الأصمعي أنشدته كذلك لخلف الأحمر فقال أصلحه

SULAMI:v2p133#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ explains God’s words as the knowledge of His book and the wonders of His wisdom.
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه : في قوله : ﴿ ما نفدت كلمات الله ﴾ قال : علم كتابه وعجائب حكمته

SULAMI:v2p133#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r2.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz says the speech of sages flows without end from wisdom because their wisdom is taught from the Lord’s inexhaustible treasuries.
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز : كلام الحكماء لا ينقطع من عيون الحكمة كما أن ماء العيون لا ينقطع عن عينه

SULAMI:v2p133#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r3.claim: Al-Junayd says continual blessings should make one love God; His pre-eternal words chose and supported the servant, called them in this life, and lead them to future felicity.
SULAMI:v2p133#3/r3.anchor: وقال الجنيد ورحمة الله عليه : كيف لا تحب سيدك وما انفككت من تواتر نعمه قط

ITQAN:v1p36/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p36/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p36/r5.claim: The classification treats al-Naml, al-Qasas, al-Ankabut, al-Rum, and Luqman as Meccan, except three Medinan verses of Luqman beginning 'If every tree on earth were pens'.
ITQAN:v1p36/r5.anchor: وسورة النمل والقصص والعنكبوت والروم ولقمان سوى ثلاث آيات منها نزلن بالمدينة ﴿ ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام ﴾

ITQAN:v2p507/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p507/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p507/r1.claim: لو is a past conditional particle, shifting a present-tense verb into the past, unlike إن, which conditions the future.
ITQAN:v2p507/r1.anchor: حرف شرط في المضي يصرف المضارع إليه بعكس إن الشرطية

ITQAN:v2p507/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p507/r2.speaker: أصحاب القول الأول
ITQAN:v2p507/r2.claim: The first view says لو only links a past condition and result and does not itself imply that either failed; Ibn Hisham rejects this as contrary to ordinary understanding.
ITQAN:v2p507/r2.anchor: أحدها أنها لا تفيده بوجه ولا تدل على امتناع الشرط ولا امتناع الجواب

ITQAN:v2p507/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p507/r3.speaker: سيبويه
ITQAN:v2p507/r3.claim: Sibawayh defines لو as what would have occurred had something else occurred: the expected event does not happen because its enabling condition is absent.
ITQAN:v2p507/r3.anchor: الثاني وهو لسيبويه قال إنها حرف لما كان سيقع لوقوع غيره أي أنها تقتضي فعلا ماضيا

ITQAN:v2p507/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p507/r4.speaker: جمهور النحاة
ITQAN:v2p507/r4.claim: The widespread grammatical view calls لو a particle of counterfactual nonoccurrence: the result fails because the condition fails; the author notes cases where the result would hold even without the condition, including 31:27.
ITQAN:v2p507/r4.anchor: الثالث وهو المشهور على ألسنة النحاة ومشى عليه المعربون أنها حرف امتناع لامتناع

ITQAN:v2p507/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p507/r5.speaker: ابن مالك
ITQAN:v2p507/r5.claim: Ibn Malik says لو asserts the nonoccurrence of what follows and that it would entail the next clause, without deciding whether the result occurs by another route; Ibn Hisham calls this the best formulation.
ITQAN:v2p507/r5.anchor: والرابع وهو لابن مالك أنها حرف يقتضي امتناع ما يليه واستلزامه لتاليه من غير تعرض لنفي التالي

ITQAN:v1p50/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p50/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p50/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas excepts Luqman's three verses beginning 'If every tree on earth were pens' from the sūra's Meccan classification.
ITQAN:v1p50/r7.anchor: لقمان استثنى منها ابن عباس ﴿ ولو أنما في الأرض ﴾ الآيات الثلاث كما تقدم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r1.speaker: أبو تمام
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r1.claim: Abū Tammām presents rare poetic ideas as finding a familiar home at the patron’s court, where what was strange becomes familiar.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r1.anchor: ولأبي تمام ، من + الطويل + : ( إليك أرحنا عازب الشعر بعدما تمهل في روض المعاني العجائب )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r2.claim: The source notes that the poet transfers the word craft from the tongue to the inner faculty, and that Ḥassān also calls the tongue a craft; the poem pictures thought as supplying a necklace.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p374/r2.anchor: أخذ لفظ الصنع من قول أبي حية : ' بأنني صنع اللسان بهن لا أتنحل ' ، ونقله إلى الضمير . وقد جعل حسان أيضا اللسان صنعا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r1.speaker: ناس من النحويين
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r1.claim: Some grammarians read innamā in the verse about forbidden acts as restrictive, equivalent in sense to mā ... illā: God forbade only the named indecencies.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r1.anchor: يقول ناس من النحويين في نحو قوله تعالى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī supports that restrictive analysis with al-Farazdaq’s line: a positive reading would make the detached pronoun ungrammatical, so the sense is that only I or my like defends their honor.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو علي في الشيرازيات : يقول ناس من النحويين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the accusative on al-maytata is the transmitted reading, though another parsing is possible; he prefers treating mā as preventing inna from governing, with innamā meaning that only carrion and blood are forbidden.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج في قوله تعالى :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r4.claim: Al-Jurjānī stresses that saying innamā can mean mā ... illā does not make the constructions interchangeable: each works in contexts where the other fails.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p252/r4.anchor: فإنهم لم يعنوا بذلك أن المعنى في هذا هو المعنى في ذلك بعينه

DAMGHANI:v1p405/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p405/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p405/r12.claim: The source lists seven further senses of kalimāt: rites, what Adam received, words of tawḥīd, God's creative wonders, Jesus, God's religion, and the Qur'an.
DAMGHANI:v1p405/r12.anchor: ك ل م على سبعة أوجه المناسك ما تلقى آدم ألفاظ التوحيد عجائب صنع الله عيسى عليه السلام دين الله القرآن

DAMGHANI:v1p408/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r4.claim: God’s words are the wonders of His making; the oceans could not exhaust them, as the parallel verse in al-Kahf states.
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r4.anchor: كلمات الله عجائب صنعه تعالى قوله تعالى في سورة لقمان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r3.claim: البحر names abundant, spacious water and is so called because of its breadth; it can also describe a horse with a broad stride.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r3.anchor: البحر : اسم للماء الغزير الواسع ، وسمي بحرا لاتساعه ، ويقال : فرس بحر ، إذا كان واسع الجري

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r4.claim: The entry cites the Prophet describing someone or something as a sea, an expression of abundance or broadness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' وإن وجدناه لبحرا '

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r5.claim: The word can describe salty water; the entry cites a poem about the earth's water turning salty and a sweet drink becoming briny.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r5.anchor: والماء [ البحر ] : الملح . ويقال أبحر إذا ملح ، قال نصيب : - وقد عاد ماء الأرض بحرا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r7.speaker: الأموي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r7.claim: Al-Awmari says البحرة means a town or locality, as in 'our town.'
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p197/r7.anchor: وقال الأموي : البحرة : البلدة . يقال هذه بحرتنا ، أي : بلدتنا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p524/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p524/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p524/r3.claim: A fourth sense is God's knowledge and wonders; another view takes the words literally because God's speech does not end.

MAJAZ:v2p128/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p128/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p128/r1.claim: He says al-baḥr here means fresh water, since salty seawater cannot grow pens; Arabs also called inland countryside a sea.
MAJAZ:v2p128/r1.anchor: مجاز البحر هاهنا الماء العذب يقال

MAJAZ:v2p128/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p128/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p128/r2.claim: He reads min baʿdihi as from behind it: seven seas flow into the freshwater sea.
MAJAZ:v2p128/r2.anchor: يمده من بعده أي من خلفه أي يسيل فيه سبعة أبحر

MAJAZ:v2p128/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p128/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p128/r3.claim: He treats the clause as compressed, with an implicit phrase: even if God’s book were written with these pens and seas, it would not be exhausted.
MAJAZ:v2p128/r3.anchor: ومجازه مجاز المختصر الذي فيه ضمير، سبيله: فكتب كتاب الله بهذه الأقلام وبهذه البحور

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads البحر accusative; one parse coordinates it with أن, making يمده its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالنصب، والباقون بالرفع. فالنصب من وجهين،

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r2.claim: A second accusative parse supplies a verb explained by يمده; waw introduces a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r2.anchor: والواو حينئذ للحال. والجملة حالية، ولم يحتج إلى ضمير رابط

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r3.claim: The estimate pictures the sea being supplied by further seas.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r3.anchor: والتقدير: ولو أن الذي في الأرض حال كون البحر ممدودا بكذا.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r4.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r4.claim: Sibawayh treats coordinated البحر as a subject phrase after لو, estimated ولو البحر.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r4.anchor: مذهب سيبويه الرفع على الابتداء، ومذهب المبرد على الفاعلية بفعل مقدر، وهما عائدان هنا. فعلى مذهب سيبويه يكون تقدير العطف: ولو البحر.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r5.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad treats البحر as subject of an omitted verb.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r5.anchor: ومذهب المبرد على الفاعلية بفعل مقدر، وهما عائدان هنا.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r6.claim: On either coordinated analysis, يمده is circumstantial to البحر.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r6.anchor: وعلى التقديرين يكون " يمده " جملة حالية من البحر.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r7.claim: Al-Shaykh says a bare noun does not directly follow لو as subject except in necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r7.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ قال: إنه لا يلي " لو " المبتدأ اسما صريحا

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r8.claim: Al-Shaykh says coordination may license what is disallowed for its first conjunct.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r8.anchor: ثم أجاب بأنه يغتفر في المعطوف ما لا يغتفر في المعطوف عليه كقولهم: " رب رجل وأخيه يقولان ذلك ".

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses البحر as subject and يمده as predicate in a circumstantial clause, framed as question and answer.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r9.anchor: والثاني: أن " البحر " مبتدأ، و " يمده " الخبر، والجملة حالية كما تقدم في جملة الاشتغال، والرابط الواو. وقد جعله الزمخشري سؤالا وجوابا.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r10.claim: وقد أغتدي والطير في وكناتها illustrates the circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r10.anchor: وأنشد: 3661 وقد أغتدي والطير في وكناتها

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r11.claim: من شجرة is circumstantial from the relative or the implicit pronoun in its prepositional relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r11.anchor: إما من الموصول، أو من الضمير المستتر في الجار الواقع صلة،

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r12.claim: أقلام is the predicate of أن.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r13.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r13.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects the claim that the predicate of أن after لو must be verbal.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r13.anchor: وفيه دليل على من يقول - كالزمخشري ومن يتعصب له من العجم - على أن خبر " أن " الواقعة بعد " لو " لا يكون اسما البتة لا جامدا ولا مشتقا

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r14.claim: A poem with عصفورة supplies a nominal predicate after أن following لو.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r15.claim: Another poem says ما أطيب العيش لو أن الفتى حجر.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27/r15.anchor: 3663 ما أطيب العيش لو أن الفتى حجر

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r1.claim: Another cited poem gives أخو الحرب as a nominal predicate after لو أن.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r1.anchor: 3664 ولو أن حيا فائت الموت فاته

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r2.claim: Al-Samin says this construction is common in Arabic.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r3.speaker: author
