SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r3.claim: This and similar verses refute the apparent view that لو means counterfactuality whose result negates its condition.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r3.anchor: هذه الآية ونحوها تبطل ظاهر قول المتقدمين في " لو " أنها حرف امتناع لامتناع

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r4.claim: Al-Samin refers readers to the opening of al-Baqara for لو.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r5.claim: Abd Allah reads وبحر indefinite; circumstantial waw licenses an indefinite subject.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r5.anchor: وهو معدود من مسوغات الابتداء بالنكرة.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r6.claim: The poem beginning سرينا ونجم قد أضاء illustrates an indefinite subject after circumstantial waw.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r6.anchor: أنشدوا: 3665 سرينا ونجم قد أضاء فمذ بدا

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r7.claim: That license refutes the claim that the indefinite reading must coordinate with أن.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r7.anchor: كأنه توهم أنه ليس ثم مسوغ

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله وأبي
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r8.claim: Abd Allah and Ubayy read تمده with feminine ت for seven seas.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبي " تمده " بالتأنيث لأجل " سبعة ".

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r9.speaker: الحسن وابن هرمز وابن مصرف
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Hurmuz, and Ibn Musrif read يمده from أمده.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r9.anchor: والحسن وابن هرمز وابن مصرف " يمده " بالياء من تحت مضمومة وكسر الميم من أمده.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the singular distributively: consider every tree so none is left for pens.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r10.anchor: أريد تفصيل الشجر وتقصيها شجرة شجرة حتى لا يبقى من جنس الشجر واحدة إلا قد بريت أقلاما

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r11.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r11.claim: Al-Shaykh explains singular for plural and indefinite for definite, like ما ننسخ من آية.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r11.anchor: وهو من وقوع المفرد موقع الجمع والنكرة موقع المعرفة، كقوله: ما ننسخ من آية

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r12.claim: Al-Samin says this removes al-Zamakhshari's distributive sense.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r12.anchor: قلت: وهذا يذهب بالمعنى الذي أبداه الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why كلمات is a limited plural and says seas cannot supply writing material for God's words.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r13.anchor: " الكلمات " جمع قلة، والموضع موضع تكثير، فهلا قيل: كلم

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r14.claim: Al-Samin calls the answer an argument by duality a fortiori.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r14.anchor: قلت: يعني أنه من باب التثنية بطريق الأولى.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r15.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r15.claim: Al-Shaykh says a sound plural with non-referential ال or annexation is general.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r15.anchor: ورده الشيخ: بأن جمع السلامة متى عرف بأل غير العهدية أو أضيف عم.

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r16.claim: Al-Samin notes disagreement on whether ال conveys generality; al-Zamakhshari may deny it.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#2/r16.anchor: قلت للناس خلاف في " أل " هل تعم أو لا؟ وقد يكون الزمخشري ممن لا يرى العموم

SAMIN-DURR:31:27#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#3/r1.speaker: حسان
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#3/r1.claim: Hassan's الجفنات الغر is a parallel: people ask why use a limited plural for praise rather than الجفان, supporting al-Zamakhshari's point.
SAMIN-DURR:31:27#3/r1.anchor: ويقولون: كيف أتى بجمع القلة في مقام المدح؟ ولم لم يقل الجفان؟ وهو تقرير لما قاله الزمخشري

ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r1.claim: The words of God do not end or run out.

ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r2.claim: The explanation answers polytheists who claimed the Qur'an's speech would run out: God's words and wisdom are inexhaustible.
ZAJJAJ:v4p200/r2.anchor: قالوا في القرآن: إن هذا كلام سينفد

ASAD-NOTES:31:27#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:27#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:27#n25/r1.claim: Asad compares the description of God's inexhaustible words with a similar passage at 18:109.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r1.claim: Luqman's statement that God's words never run out belongs to the surah's argument for revelation and the Qur'an against those who deny it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r1.anchor: وفيها جميعاً احتجاج للقرآن ردّاً على جدل المكذبين، فهي تستهل بعد الأحرف المقطعة، بتقرير تنزيله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r2.claim: The seven Hawamim came consecutively in revelation order and also stand consecutively in the Qur'anic arrangement: surahs 40–46.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r2.anchor: ثم نزلت الحواميم السبع متتالية في ترتيب نزولها (60: 66) متتالية كذلك في ترتيب المصحف (40: 46)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r3.claim: Each Hawamim surah opens with حم, while al-Shura adds عسق; after these letters they affirm revelation from the Mighty, Wise God in clear Arabic.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p171/r3.anchor: وكلها تبدأ بحرفى "حم" ومعهما في سورة الشورى: "عسق" وفيها جميعاً احتجاج للقرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r1.claim: She says inherited scholarly standing and the honored place of Muslim women in Islamic history emboldened her to enter a demanding field dominated by earlier scholars.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r1.anchor: لولا نسب لى فى الشيوخ عريق، لتهيبت التصدى لهذا الموضوع الدقيق الصعب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r2.claim: Her lifelong Qur'anic study began under her father and advanced under Amin al-Khuli, who guided her for a third of a century.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r2.anchor: وفي المدرسة القرآنية كانت تلمذتي الطويلة التي تولاها أبي في مراحلها الأولى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r3.claim: Al-Khuli's strict method requires tracing every form of a Qur'anic word and studying each subject or stylistic feature across parallels and contexts, locally and throughout the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r3.anchor: منهجه الدقيق الصارم الذى لا يجيز لنا أن نفسر كلمة من كلمات الله تعالى دون استقراء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r4.claim: Her work on Qur'anic exegesis led her to study rhetorical inimitability and systematically ask why native Arab masters of eloquence could not produce a comparable surah.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p11/r4.anchor: تجلى لي من أسراره الباهرة ما لفتني إلى موقف العرب الأصلاء من المعجزة القرآنية في عصر المبعث

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r1.claim: Al-Sharif al-Murtada observed that the Arab Prophet's miracle was linked to eloquence, the central art of his people.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r1.anchor: إلى ارتباط معجزة النبي العربي بمكان البيان في قومه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r2.claim: She proposes that prophetic miracles accompanied humanity's development from primitive stages toward maturity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r2.anchor: مما هدى إليه النظر في تاريخ الأديان المقارن من أن معجزات الأنبياء سايرت تدرج البشرية في مراحل تطورها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r3.claim: Moses came as humanity moved beyond magic; his miracle defeated contemporary magicians and showed skeptics that his sign exceeded human ability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r3.anchor: فكانت معجزته التي غلبت أفانين السحرة في زمنه وتحدت براعة المهرة منهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r5.claim: Jesus came in an age of hero worship; his extraordinary signs surpassed heroic feats to establish his prophethood and guide people from hero worship to monotheism.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p55/r5.anchor: جاءت معجزة المسيح الخارقة، لكي يؤمن الناس بنبوته المؤيدة بما يجاوز خوارقهم البطولية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r5.claim: The Prophet is urged to be patient, entrust the disbelievers’ fate to God, and disregard their demands for signs because abundant signs are already present.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r5.anchor: he should now consign their matter to God; He will decide about their fate; he should not pay heed to them if they are demanding signs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r6.claim: Even if all trees became pens and the seas, multiplied by seven, became ink, they still could not record all of God’s signs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r6.anchor: even then all of God’s signs cannot be written.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r3.claim: The “words” are God's signs, which testify to His being, attributes, power and wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r3.anchor: The word ُت ٰمِلَک refers to those signs of God which bear witness to His being and attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r4.claim: Calling these signs God's “words” is apt because each manifests His command kun and displays itself through existence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r4.anchor: every sign is a manifestation of God’s command of kun

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r5.claim: God is not obscure or unknown: the abundance of His signs leaves no excuse for becoming confused and worshiping a random stone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r5.anchor: God is not someone vague and unknown so that people get confused about Him and start worshiping whichever stone they come across.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r6.claim: Islahi notes that this image had already appeared in Sūrah al-Kahf, at 18:109.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r6.anchor: What is stated in this verse, has already appeared in Sūrah Kahf in the following words:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r7.claim: Even if the earth's trees became pens and the seas, including seven more, became ink, God's signs could not all be written down.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r7.anchor: even then all of them cannot be recorded in writing.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r8.claim: The innumerable signs demonstrate that the creator is powerful and wise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p122/r8.anchor: These signs show that the creator of this universe is powerful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r1.claim: God's might and wisdom are basic attributes from which the Qur'an adduces monotheism, prophethood and the Hereafter; the universe's signs invite people to their implications.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r1.anchor: These three beliefs form the basic issues discussed by the Qur’ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r2.claim: The noun “ink,” parallel to “pens,” is omitted from the verse's wording.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r2.anchor: the word ادَدِمٌ parallel to ٌم َلَاۡقَا is suppressed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r3.claim: Islahi calls the image in 18:109 factual rather than exaggerated: even ink made from the sea cannot record the signs within it, let alone the universe; scientific discoveries remain a drop in that vastness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p123/r3.anchor: what is stated is no exaggeration. It is a statement of fact.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r1.claim: These readers read البحر nominative; Abu Amr alone reads it accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: والبحر رفعا. وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r2.claim: Abu Amr reads البحر accusative, coordinated with ما, with يمده as its predicate.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r3.claim: The accusative coordinates البحر with ما, subject of إن; the nominative begins a new sentence describing the sea's state.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r3.anchor: إذا عطفت البحر على اسم إن فنصبته كان خبره يمده، والراجع إلى البحر الضمير المنصوب

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda calls the wording an abbreviated construction, like saying that writing God's Book with these pens and seas would not exhaust it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هذا مختصر سبيله كسبيل لو كتب كتاب الله بهذه الأقلام والبحر ما نفد كلام الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r5.claim: Al-Farisi understands the hypothetical writing to concern what is in God's decree; the written amount would end before the decreed content.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: المراد بذلك والله أعلم: ما في المقدر دون ما خرج منه إلى الوجود

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r6.claim: Qatada says the pens and seven seas would run out before God's marvels, wisdom, creation, and knowledge were exhausted.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: يقول: لو كان شجر الأرض أقلاما، ومع البحر سبعة أبحر، إذا لانكسرت الأقلام

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r7.claim: The reading permits omitted actions recovered from context, as in the sea splitting after Moses is told to strike it and the other examples cited.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r7.anchor: ونحو هذا من الجمل قد تحذف لدلالة الكلام عليها، كقوله تعالى : وأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر فانفلق

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p457#2/r8.claim: Abu Zayd uses أمددت for supplying people or a commander with money or troops, and describes one river as feeding another.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p459/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p459/r1.speaker: بعض أهل النظر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p459/r1.claim: One speculative interpreter says the inexhaustible thing is God's wisdom, wondrous workmanship, and its perfection, rather than speech itself.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p459/r1.anchor: ليس هذا على الكلام ولكن المراد أن وجه الحكمة وتأمل عجيب الصنعة وإتقانها لا ينفد، وليس المراد الكلام.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r1.speaker: يونس والأصمعي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r1.claim: Yūnus reports السوق pronounced الصوق; al-Aṣmaʿī recounts a dispute over سقر with ṣād or sīn resolved by a passerby saying زقر, illustrating dialectal sound variation.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r1.anchor: في السوق: الصوق، وروينا عن الأصمعي، قال: تنازع رجلان في السقر،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وطلحة بن مصرف
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read وبحر يمده, with بحر indefinite.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r3.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad reads والبحر مداده, presenting the sea as the ink.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r4.speaker: الأعرج والحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r4.claim: Al-Aʿraj and al-Hasan read والبحر يمده with ḍamma on yāʾ.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r5.claim: Ibn Jinnī finds an ellipsis in the verse: its sense is that God’s words would be written by those pens and would not run out; the omitted clause is clear from context.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r5.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: في إعراب هذه الآية نظر؛ وذلك أن هناك حذفا، فتقديره: فكتب بذلك كلمات الله ما نفدت،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r6.claim: With indefinite بحر in the nominative, Ibn Jinnī takes it as a new subject with an omitted predicate, There is also a sea; it cannot coordinate with أقلام because the sea supplies ink, as Jaʿfar’s reading shows.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r6.anchor: وأما رفع "بحر" فالابتداء، وخبره محذوف، أي: وهناك بحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r7.claim: Definite البحر may be coordinated with the syntactic position of أن and its noun; the accusative reading reported from Abū ʿAmr instead coordinates it with ما, as in أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r7.anchor: فأما رفع "البحر" فإن شئت كان معطوفا على موضع

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r8.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r8.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r8.claim: Ṭalḥa’s indefinite nominative وبحر يمده proves that the wāw may be circumstantial: there is also a sea that is supplied by seven more seas.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r8.anchor: ويشهد بجواز كون الواو حالا هنا قراءة طلحة بن مصرف: "وبحر يمده"، أي: وهناك بحر يمده

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r9.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r9.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p169/r9.claim: With ḍamma on yāʾ, يُمده evokes reinforcement and supply, like one river fed by another or an army reinforced with troops.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r1.claim: Raising al-baḥr coordinates with the clause before inna or begins a new clause; the author cites “one group He covered … and one group” as a parallel.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن رفع أنه رده على ما قبل دخول إن عليها أو استأنفه بالواو

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r2.claim: Accusative al-baḥr coordinates with the noun of inna; although Abu ʿAmr usually raises a conjunct after its predicate, here law requires a response, and the predicate ends at “God's words would not be exhausted.”
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p286#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن نصب أنه رده على اسم إن فإن قيل فإن من شرط أبي عمرو أن يرفع المعطوف على إن بعد تمام الخبر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r1.claim: Abu Amr alone reads والبحر in the accusative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وحده ﴿ والبحر ﴾ نصبا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r2.speaker: الباقون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r2.claim: The remaining readers read والبحر in the nominative.

NASHR:v2p346/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p346/r5.speaker: البصريان
NASHR:v2p346/r5.claim: The two Basrans read the rāʾ of al-baḥr with accusative inflection; the other readers use the nominative.
NASHR:v2p346/r5.anchor: فقرأ البصريان بنصب الراء، وقرأ الباقون بالرفع

QIRAAT-ER:31:27:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:27:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:27:10#1/r1.claim: The accusative al-baḥra can be parsed as object of an omitted verb or coordinated with the ism of anna, keeping the sea within the original clause.
QIRAAT-ER:31:27:10#1/r1.anchor: Accusative reading (naṣb): al-baḥra as object of a deleted verb or maʿṭūf on ism anna

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#2/r1.claim: Qatāda reports that polytheists said the Qurʾān’s words would soon run out or end, and this verse was revealed in response.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة أن المشركين قالوا في القرآن إن هذا الكلام يوشك أن ينفذ يوشك أن ينقطع فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p405#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p405#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p405#2/r13.claim: The word al-qalam simply means a pen.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r15.claim: Although the created world is finite, the wonders of God’s power and knowledge have no end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r15.anchor: وكان ذلك متناهيا، بين أن في قدرته وعلمه عجائب لا نهاية لها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r16.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r16.claim: Al-Mubarrad parses the clause after law as nominative in the subject position, with the sense ‘if it occurred or existed.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r16.anchor: وأن بعد لو في موضع رفع على الفاعلية، أي لو وقع أو ثبت على رأي المبرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r17.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r17.claim: Other grammarians parse the clause after law as an initial noun phrase whose predicate is omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r17.anchor: أو في موضع مبتدأ محذوف الخبر على رأي غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r18.claim: Min shajaratin explains mā; it is analyzed circumstantially from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, while the estimated clause makes ‘pens’ the predicate of anna.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r18.anchor: ومن شجرة: تبيين لما، وهو في التقرير في موضع الحال من الضمير الذي في الجار والمجرور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r19.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s claim that anna after lawlā must have a verbal predicate; he says Arabic usage abundantly disproves it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r19.anchor: وفيه دليل على بطلان دعوى الزمخشري وبعض العجم ممن ينصر قوله: إن خبر أن الجائية بعد لولا يكون اسما جامدا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: After إن, a following noun may be raised as a new subject because إن only emphasizes the preceding clause; Sībawayh prefers this analysis over raising it on a hidden pronoun in the predicate.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: يكون محمولا على الابتداء لأن معنى إن زيدا منطلق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: A second noun may instead be accusative by coordination with إن’s noun, as in إن زيدا منطلق وعمرا ظريف; Sībawayh cites ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده as a parallel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: منطلق وعمرا ظريف فحملته على قوله عز وجل ^ ( ولو أن ما فى ا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r1.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies an omitted ثابت as the predicate of أنما, inferred from the conditional construction and the particle's sense of established fact.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r1.anchor: بقرينة كون ( أن ) دالة على الثبوت والتحقق وإلى هذا ذهب المبرد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r2.claim: Sibawayh treats the clause as a subject that needs no overt predicate because its subject and predicate are stated afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r2.anchor: وقال سيبويه : إن ذلك مبتدأ مستغن عن الخبر لذكر المسند والمسند إليه بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r3.claim: One analysis makes the construction a subject whose predicate is estimated before it; Ibn ʿAsfur instead places the estimated predicate after it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r3.anchor: وقيل : مبتدأ خبره مقدر قبله وقال إبن عصفور : بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r4.speaker: ابن عصفور
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAsfur locates the omitted predicate after the subject; the phrase ما في الأرض is the noun of أن, and من شجرة explains ما or its locative pronoun as a circumstantial phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r4.anchor: و ( ما في الأرض ) أسم أن و ( من شجرة )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r5.claim: The author parses أقلام as the predicate of أن and allows من شجرة to explain either ما or its pronoun in the locative phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r5.anchor: فهو في موضع الحال منها أو منه أي ولو ثبت أن الذي أستقر في الأرض كائنا من شجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan says the construction disproves al-Zamakhsharī's claim that an أن following conditional لو must have a verbal predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r6.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وفيه دليل دعوى الزمخشري وبعض العجم ممن ينصر قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r7.claim: The author answers that the alleged verb requirement applies only when the predicate is a derived adjective, so the inanimate noun أقلام and the cited nominal predicates do not refute it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r7.anchor: وتعقب بأن إشتراط كون خبرها فعلا إنما هو إذا كان مشتقا فلا يرد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r8.claim: Two cited poems use nominal predicates after لو أن; لو أنهم بادون is set aside because its لو expresses a wish rather than a conditional.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر : ولو أنها عصفورة لحسبتها مسومة تدعو عبيدا وأزنما

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r9.claim: شجرة means every tree here: an indefinite can be universal after a conditional when context calls for it, as in the cited Qurʾanic expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r9.anchor: والمراد بشجرة كل شجرة والنكرة قد تعم في الإثبات إذا أقتضى المقام ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r10.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās illustrates the force of a generic singular by answering that one date is better than one locust when asked about expiation for killing a locust in pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r10.anchor: وقول إبن عباس رضي الله عنهما لبعض أهل الشام وقد سأله عن المحرم إذا قتل جرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r11.claim: Each tree supplies many pens through its parts or branches, yielding the sense that all the trees' parts or branches become pens.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r11.anchor: وكون كل شجرة أقلاما بإعتبار الأجزاء أو الأغصان فيؤل المعنى إلى لو أن أجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r12.claim: The singular شجرة is better than أشجار or شجر because it avoids implying a distributive assignment of one pen to each tree, which would weaken the hyperbole.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r12.anchor: على أشجار أو شجر لأن الكلام عليه أبعد عن إعتبار التوزيع بأن تكون كل شجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan calls this a singular indefinite used with plural, definite force, as in several Qurʾanic and Arabic examples; here it can mean trees generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97/r13.anchor: وفي البحر أن هذا مما وقع فيه المفرد موقع الجمع والنكرة موقع المعرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the singular شجرة unfolds the trees one by one until not a single tree of the species remains outside the image.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : إنه قال سبحانه ( شجرة ) على التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.claim: The author objects that a lone singular does not normally convey distributive repetition; Arabic expresses that sense by repeating the noun, as in رجلا رجلا.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.anchor: وتعقب بأن إفادة المفرد التفصيل بدون تكرار غير معهود والمعهود إفادته ذلك بالتكرير

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.claim: أقلام is a plural of paucity although the context suggests abundance, because no other familiar plural of قلم is in circulation; قلام is uncommon.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.anchor: وإختيار جمع القلة في ( أقلام ( مع أن الأنسب للمقام جمع الكثرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.claim: Al-Baḥr most naturally denotes the encircling ocean, the known and greatest single sea; a generic sea is possible, but the known ocean makes the image stronger.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.anchor: والبحر ( أي المحيط فأل للعهد لأنه المتبادر ولأنه الفرد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.claim: من بعده can mean after the ocean's supply is exhausted, or alternatively from behind it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.anchor: يمده من بعده ( اي من بعد نفاذه وقيل من ورائه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.claim: The seven additional seas are imagined as each matching the ocean in extent, encirclement, and water; seven signifies abundance rather than exactly seven.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.anchor: سبعة أبحر ( مفروضة كل منها مثله في السعة والإحاطة وكثرة الماء والمراد بالسبعة الكثرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.claim: The author adduces the report that a believer eats in one stomach and an unbeliever in seven as an example where seven conveys multiplicity.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.anchor: كما في قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : المؤمن يأكل في معي واحد والكافر يأكل في سبعة أمعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.claim: Seven is chosen as a complete and symbolically weighty number, familiar from the heavens, planets, regions, and days of the week; this gives the image more grandeur than seventy.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.anchor: وأخاتيرت لها لأنها عدد تام كما عرفت عند الكلام في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.claim: أبحر is formally a plural of paucity, fitting the word سبعة, while both are figuratively used for great multiplicity.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.anchor: ولما لم تكن موضوعة في الأصل لذلك بل للعدد المعروف القليل جاء تمييزها أبحر بلفظ القلة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r10.claim: The wording يمده evokes continuously replenishing an inkpot: it implies ink without saying مداد and its imperfect form pictures unceasing supply.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r10.anchor: لكن جيء بما في النظم الجليل لأن يمده يغني عن ذكر المداد لأنه من قولك : مد الدواة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r11.claim: The image turns the ocean into an inkpot with seven matching seas continually pouring ink into it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r11.anchor: فأفاد النظم الجليل جعل البحر المحيط بمنزلة الدواة وجعل أبحر سبعة مثله مملوءة مدادا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r12.claim: On the preferred parsing, البحر is nominative as subject and يمده is its predicate; the clause is circumstantial, linked by واو الحال to the relative phrase or its pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r12.anchor: ورفع ( البحر ) على ما أستظهره أبو حيان فيه على الإبتداء وجملة يمده خبره والواو للحال

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats such circumstantial nominal clauses as adverbial in meaning, so their relation to the preceding clause resembles a ظرف even without an explicit pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r13.anchor: وأشار الزمخشري إلى أن هذه الجملة وما أشبهها كقوله : وقد أغتدي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r14.claim: The author finds the circumstantial link sufficient through واو الحال; he rejects the need to posit a pronoun transferred from an understood adverb.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r14.anchor: نعم الحق أن الربط بالواو كاف عن الضمير ولا يحتاج معه إلى تكلف هذه المؤنة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r15.claim: Other parses make the circumstantial clause modify الأرض through its sense of established location, or let البحر's ال stand for a pronoun under the Kufan analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r15.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الجملة حالا من الأرض والعامل فيه معنى الإستقرار والرابط ما سمعت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's analysis requires من شجرة to explain the pronoun referring to ما, avoiding an unrelated phrase splitting the relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p97#2/r16.anchor: قال في الكشف : ولا بد أن يجعل ( من شجرة ) بيانا للضمير

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r1.claim: Al-Ṭībī says that if ال substitutes for the pronoun annexed to الأرض, البحر generalizes to all seas and makes the seven seas separate from Earth's sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r1.anchor: وقال الطيبي : إن البحر على ذلك يعم جميع الأبحر لقرينة الإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r2.claim: The author sees no real distinction between the analyses and favors the familiar ocean: annexation most naturally marks definiteness, and that ocean encircles the whole Earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r2.anchor: ورد بأنه لا فرق بينهما بل كون بحرها للعهد أظهر لأن العهد أصل الإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also permits البحر to coordinate with the syntactic sense of أن and its complement, with يمده as a circumstantial clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r3.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون رفعه بالعطف على محل أن ومعمولها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r4.claim: The author objects that coordinating across the elided predicate's evidential trigger makes the omitted verb's relation to the coordinate unclear; a reply allows more freedom in a dependent coordinate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r4.anchor: وتعقب بأن الدال على الفعل المحذوف هو أن وخبره على ما قرر في بابه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r5.claim: On the coordination analysis, البحر coordinates with the singular verbal noun that serves as subject of ثابت, not with an entire sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r5.anchor: إذ الظاهر أن المعطوف عليه إنما هو المصدر الواقع فاعلا لثبت وهو مفرد لا جملة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r6.claim: A subject-first analysis would put an overt noun directly after conditional لو, which Abu Hayyan allows only as poetic necessity, citing a verse about thirst.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r6.anchor: إذ يصير التقدير ولو البحر وذلك على ما قال أبو حيان لا يجوز إلا في ضرورة شعر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r7.claim: Another proposal makes البحر a subject, treats the clause as a predicate with واو المعية, and puts the whole clause in the accusative as a مفعول معه; the author calls it far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r7.anchor: وجوز كون الرفع على الإبتداء وجملة ( يمده ) خبر المبتدأ والواو واو المعية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r8.claim: A proposed independent answer to an imagined question about the ink is rejected because beginning an answer with واو is not established in this use.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r8.anchor: وجوز كون الواو على ذلك للإستئناف بياني كأنه قيل : ما المداد حينئذ فقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r9.claim: The author also dismisses the claim that واو introduces an answer to a debating question, judging that grammatical defense unreliable.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99/r9.anchor: وتعقب بأن اقتران الجواب بالواو وإن كانت إستئنافية غير معهود

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.speaker: البصريان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.claim: The two Basran readers pronounce البحر in the accusative, coordinating it with the noun of أن; يمده then predicates that the sea is replenished by seven seas.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ البصريان ( والبحر ) بالنصب على أنه معطوف على أسم أن

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib rejects taking يمده as a circumstantial clause because that restricts an inanimate subject and leaves البحر without a predicate; أقلام already predicates the first noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r2.anchor: قال إبن الحاجب في أماليه : ولا يستقيم أن يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.claim: Another parse makes the accusative البحر coordinate with the omitted verb ثابت under لو, leaving يمده without a syntactic position.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون منصوبا على شريطة التفسير عطفا على الفعل المحذوف أعني ثبت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.speaker: عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads وبحر as an indefinite nominative; Ibn Jinnī supplies an omitted predicate, while the author says يمده can straightforwardly be its predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله ( وبحر ) بالتنكير والرفع وخرج ذلك إبن جني على أنه مبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.claim: On ʿAbd Allāh's reading, the author prefers making يمده the predicate of the indefinite subject, with no need to posit an omitted predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p99#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر على تقدير كونه مبتدأ جعل الجملة خبره ولا حاجة إلى جعل خبره محذوفا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read تمده with feminine تاء, from mad, as in the common reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r1.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود وأبي ( تمده ) بتاء التأنيث

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن وابن مصرف وابن هرمز
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muṣarrif, and Ibn Hurmuz read يمده with a ḍamma on ياء, from the causative امداد.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r2.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود أيضا والحسن وإبن مصرف وإبن هرمز ( يمده ) بضم الياء التحتية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r3.speaker: ابن الشيخ
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r3.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the forms يمدّ and يُمدّ are two dialect variants with the same meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r3.anchor: قال إبن الشيخ : يمد بفتح فضم ويمد بضم فكسر لغتان بمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r4.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r4.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad reads والبحر مداده, meaning the ink with which one writes; Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies مداد as a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r4.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( والبحر مداده ) أي ما يكتب به من الحبر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r5.claim: ما نفدت كلمات الله is the جواب لو; an omitted scenario is understood from context, a concise ellipsis contrasting unbounded divine words with finite pens and ink.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r5.anchor: ما نفدت كلمات الله ( جواب ( لو ) وفي الكلام إختصار يسمى حذف إيجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r6.claim: If the trees became pens and the sea plus seven seas became ink and wrote God's words, the words would not run out, while the pens and ink would.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r6.anchor: وكتبت بتلك الأقلام وبذلك المداد كلمات الله تعالى ما نفدت لعدم تناهيها ونفد تلك الأقلام

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r7.claim: The author compares the omitted wording to the concise ellipsis in the expiation verse: if one shaved the head to remove harm, then expiation is due.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r7.anchor: ونظير ذلك في الإشتمال على إيجاز الحذف قوله تعالى : ( أؤ به أذى من رأسه ففدية )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r8.claim: In the interpretation tied to the reported occasion, God's words mean His knowledge and wisdom; this reading answers the question about how much knowledge people received.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r8.anchor: والمراد بكلماته تعالى كلمات علمه سبحانه وحكمته جل شأنه وهو الذي يقتضيه سبب النزول

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r9.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r9.claim: ʿIkrima reports that the People of the Book asked the Prophet about the spirit, then objected that the claim of little knowledge conflicted with the Torah's wisdom; this verse was revealed in reply.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r9.anchor: أخرج إبن جرير عن عكرمة قال : سأل أهل الكتاب رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r10.claim: One account has Jews ask the Prophet directly, suggesting a Medinan setting; another has Jews instruct a Quraysh delegation, which supports a Meccan setting.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r10.anchor: وظاهر هذا أن اليهود قالوا ذلك له عليه الصلاة والسلام مشافهة وهو ظاهر في أن الآية مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r11.claim: A further narrative places the spirit question in Mecca and a later challenge by Jewish scholars after the migration; the Prophet answers that Torah knowledge is little beside God's knowledge and that wisdom is much good.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r11.anchor: وفي رواية أنه نزل بمكة قوله تعالى : ( ويسألونك )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes God's words as His decreed acts and wonders, brought into being by كن فيكون; calling them words uses cause for effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r12.anchor: وقيل : المراد بها مقدوراته جل وعلا وعجائبه عزوجل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r13.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r13.claim: The Imam prefers the decreed acts and wonders interpretation because it more clearly follows the preceding statement that everything in heaven and earth belongs to God, then signals the unbounded scope of His dominion.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r13.anchor: وهذا ما أختاره الإمام في المراد بكلماته تعالى إلا أن في إنطباقه على سبب النزول خفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r14.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r14.claim: Abū Muslim understands the words as God's promised reward for obedience and threatened punishment for disobedience, showing that more of His dominion remains unseen than has appeared.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r14.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم المراد بها ما وعد سبحانه به أهل طاعته من الثواب وما أوعد جل شأنه به أهل معصيته

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r15.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r15.claim: Qatāda reports that polytheists said the revelation would soon run out; the verse answers them, although this reading has a weak connection to the surrounding verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r15.anchor: بناء على ما أخرج عبدالرزاق وإبن جرير وإبن المنذر وغيرهم عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r16.claim: The feminine sound plural كلمات is formally a plural of paucity, implying that even a small number of God's words cannot be exhausted, let alone a great number.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r16.anchor: وإيثار الجمع المؤنث السالم بناء على أنه كجمع المذكر جمع قلة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r17.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r17.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ما نفد كلام الله without feminine تاء and uses the singular كلام instead of كلمات.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r17.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( ما نفد ) بغير تاء ( كلام الله ) بدل كلمات الله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r18.claim: The closing attributes explain why God's words cannot be exhausted: nothing can overcome Him, and nothing falls outside His knowledge and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p100/r18.anchor: إن الله عزيز ( لا يعجزه جل شأنه شيء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r1.claim: Where أن can occur, أنما can also occur; the clause after أنما is its complement, like the clause after the relative الذي, and أنما does not govern it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r1.anchor: اعلم أن كل موضع تقع فيه أن تقع فيه أنما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r2.claim: The Qur'anic phrase يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد illustrates أنما after a clause where أن إلهكم إله واحد would also work.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r3.claim: Ibn al-Itnaba's verse uses أنما in a dependent construction where an أن clause could replace it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر ابن الإطنابة # % أبلغ الحارث

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r4.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r4.claim: Al-Khalil says إنما is not a noun; it is non-governing and must introduce an independent clause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r4.anchor: فأما إنما فلا تكون اسما وإنما هي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r5.claim: Thus وجدتك إنما أنت صاحب كل خنى is valid as an independent clause after وجدتك, while وجدتك أنك صاحب كل خنى is invalid in that construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r5.anchor: أنك صاحب كل خنى لم يجز ذلك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r6.claim: أنما is also acceptable in وجد خبره أنما يجالس أهل الخبث because the clause identifies the same matter as the preceding expression.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r6.anchor: وتقول وجدت خبره أنما يجالس أهل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r7.claim: Kuthayr's verse supplies a further example of إنما introducing an independent clause rather than functioning as a noun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإنماوأنما)#501/r7.anchor: وقال كثير # % أراني ولا كفران لله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r2.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r2.claim: The commentators say the verse was revealed in Mecca in connection with 17:85: after the Prophet’s migration, Jewish scholars asked whether “you have been given little knowledge” meant them or the Prophet’s people. He said it meant everyone; they appealed to the Torah’s all-encompassing knowledge and challenged him to reconcile it with the “great good” of wisdom in 2:269, so this verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت بمكة، قوله سبحانه وتعالى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r3.claim: Qatada says the polytheists claimed that the Qur’an and what Muhammad brought would soon run out; the image of trees as pens answers them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: إن المشركين قالوا: إن القرآن وما يأتي به محمد يوشك أن ينفد فينقطع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو، يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r4.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read “the sea” in the accusative, coordinating it with “whatever is on earth.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب: "والبحر" بالنصب عطفا على

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r5.speaker: الباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r5.claim: The other readers put “the sea” in the nominative as a new sentence.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r6.claim: The sea is replenished and poured into by the additional waters.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r7.claim: “After it” means in addition to the first sea, behind it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r8.claim: The ellipsis means that if the trees were made into pens and the sea plus seven more seas used to write God’s words, His words would not be exhausted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r8.anchor: وفي الآية اختصار تقديره: ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r9.claim: The inexhaustible words of God accord with His might and wisdom.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r9.anchor: ما نفدت كلمات الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r10.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r10.claim: Ata ibn Yasar dates this verse to Medina, whereas others say it is Meccan; they say Quraysh’s delegation was told by the Jews to ask the Prophet about it while he was still in Mecca.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p292/r10.anchor: وهذه الآية على قول عطاء بن يسار مدنية، وعلى قول غيره مكية،

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r8.claim: The hypothetical makes every individual tree a pen; the singular shajara is used while distributing the claim across individual trees.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r8.anchor: ولو ثبت كون الأشجار أقلاما، وتوحيد { شجرة } لأن المراد

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r9.claim: The vast surrounding sea is extended with seven more seas as ink; madduhu conveys supplying the ink, as when one extends an inkpot.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r9.anchor: والبحر المحيط بسعته مدادا ممدودا بسبعة أبحر

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r10.claim: Bayḍāwī gives several parses: raising the sea by coordination with the clause after anna, as a new subject, or as a circumstantial clause; the Basrans also allow accusative coordination or an implied verb explained by yamudduhu.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r10.anchor: ورفعه للعطف على محل أن ومعموليها وبمده حال

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r11.claim: The passage is also read tamudduhu or yamudduhu, with feminine tāʾ or masculine yāʾ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r1.claim: Even writing God's words with all those pens and seas would not exhaust them; the plural of paucity emphasizes that the resources cannot suffice even for a little, much less much.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r1.anchor: بكتبها بتلك الأقلام بذلك المداد وإيثار جمع القلة للإشعار بأن ذلك لا يفي بالقليل

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r2.claim: God is invincible, and nothing falls outside His knowledge and wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r2.anchor: حكيم } لا يخرج عن علمه وحكمته أمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r3.claim: Bayḍāwī says the verse answers Jews who asked the Prophet, or instructed Quraysh envoys to ask him, about the statement that people were given little knowledge; they said the Torah contains knowledge of everything.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:27-28/r3.anchor: والآية جواب لليهود سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو أمروا وفد قريش

BINTSHATI:v2p7/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r1.claim: After years of contemplation, the author found Qur’anic rhetorical secrets difficult to express adequately and hesitated to publish until she had devoted her full effort, while recognizing that the subject exceeds human capacity.
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r1.anchor: فكنت كلما اجتليت باهر أسراره البيانية، ألفيت من الصعب أن أقدمها على النحو الذي يفي بخلالها

BINTSHATI:v2p7/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r2.claim: The method rigorously surveys each Qur’anic word across all its occurrences and compares stylistic features with parallels throughout the Qur’an.
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r2.anchor: بضوابطه الصارمة التي تأخذنا باستقراء اللفظ القرآني في كل مواضع وروده، للوصوص إلى دلالته

BINTSHATI:v2p7/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r3.claim: The analysis considers a feature in its immediate verse and sūra as well as in the whole muṣḥaf to uncover its rhetorical purpose.
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r3.anchor: وتدبر سياقها الخاص في الآية والسورة، ثم سياقها العام في المصحف كله، التماساً لسرها البياني

BINTSHATI:v2p7/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r4.claim: Arabic dictionaries and tafsīr serve the method, which seeks a word’s shared semantic core across its different usages.
BINTSHATI:v2p7/r4.anchor: نحاول أن ندرك حسن العربية للألفاظ التي نتدبرها من النص القرآني، عن طريق لمح الدلالة المشتركة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r13.claim: Even if every earthly tree became a pen and the sea, supplied by seven further seas, became ink, God's words would not be exhausted before the pens and ink ran out.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r14.claim: The singular شجرة is distributive and exhaustive: each tree in the earth is imagined as a pen.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r14.anchor: ودل على الاستغراق وتقصى كل فرد فرد من الجنس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r15.claim: The Basran reading puts البحر in the accusative, construed as ولو أن البحر, while the nominative reading makes it a new clause with the sea supplying more ink.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r15.anchor: وعلى قراءة البصريين بالنصب التقدير : ولو أن البحر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r16.claim: God's words are inexhaustible; creative acts follow those words, so every word brings a matter into being, as the verse about His command to say كن explains.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r16.anchor: فلا تكون كلمة إلا الأحداث شأن من الشؤون

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r17.claim: The inability to exhaust even the few words explicitly mentioned proves a fortiori that the whole of God's words cannot be exhausted.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r17.anchor: بالعجز عن ذلك القليل فيفهم العجز عن الكلم من باب الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r18.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: mentioning pens implies their omitted ink, and the seven seas imply seven trees in the imagined supply of pens.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r18.anchor: ذكر الأقلام دليلا على حذف مدادها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r19.claim: Seven seas is hyperbole for great abundance, and أبحر uses a small plural for many; by contrast, كلمات retains the small plural's literal sense to make the incapacity to count even a little striking.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r19.anchor: أن المراد بالسبعة المبالغة في الكثرة لا حقيقتها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r20.claim: God is irresistible and His decisions cannot be undone; no creature has knowledge or wisdom beyond what He grants, and these attributes answer denial of His power and resurrection wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r20.anchor: ولا حكمة لأحد منهم إلا بمقدار ما اورثه

DURR-FULL:v6p527/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r1.claim: The account recounts that Jews asked about stoning; Ibn Surya admitted it was prescribed in the Torah, and the Prophet applied the ruling. They then challenged how the Torah could contain God's judgment while its knowledge was called little, invoking 5:43 and 17:85.
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r1.anchor: ما تجدون في التوراة قال: لولا أنك نشدتني بما نشدتني به ما أخبرتك أجد فيها الرجم

DURR-FULL:v6p527/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r2.claim: The verse answers the challenge: even if all creatures wrote with every tree and sea, all pens would break and seas dry while God's words remained; the Torah contains only a little of His judgments relative to His limitless speech.
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r2.anchor: كلام الله كما هو لا ينقص ولكنكم أوتيتم التوراة فيها شيء من حكم الله وذلك في حكم الله قليل

DURR-FULL:v6p527/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that a man challenged Muhammad's claims to wisdom and the Quran while the questioner had the Torah; the verse was revealed to show that God's knowledge exceeds that amount.
DURR-FULL:v6p527/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما شاء الله أن يقول فقال رجل

DURR-FULL:v6p528/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r1.claim: The response means that the knowledge humans have received is much by their own measure, but little beside God's knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r1.anchor: {وما أوتيتم من العلم} فهو كثير لكم لقولكم قليل عندي

DURR-FULL:v6p528/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r2.claim: Ikrima says the People of the Book asked about the Spirit, were told their knowledge was little, and objected that they had the Torah and wisdom, which Scripture calls much good; this verse then came down.
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: سأل أهل الكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح

DURR-FULL:v6p528/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r3.claim: Qatada says the polytheists claimed this discourse would soon run out; the verse answers that pens and seven additional seas would be exhausted before God's wonders, wisdom, and knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: قال المشركون: إنما هذا كلام يوشك أن ينفد فنزلت {ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام}

DURR-FULL:v6p528/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the Jewish leader Hayy ibn Akhtab posed a contradiction between their having wisdom and the Jews being given little knowledge; this verse and 18:109 were revealed in reply.
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه قال: قال حي بن أخطب: يا محمد تزعم أنك أوتيت الحكمة

DURR-FULL:v6p528/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r5.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r5.claim: Abu al-Jawza explains that if every earthly tree became a pen and the seas became ink, the water would run out and the pens break before God's words did.
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r5.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام} يقول: لو كان كل شجرة في الأرض أقلاما

DURR-FULL:v6p528/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet recited البحر in the nominative (rafʿ) in the phrase about the sea being replenished.
DURR-FULL:v6p528/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قرأ (والبحر يمده) رفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r4.claim: The surah answers those who oppose the Quran here and onward, then ends by warning against Satan’s summons and false soothsayer claims to know the unseen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r4.anchor: وانتظم في هذه السورة الرد على المعارضين للقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r7.claim: Earlier assertions of God’s knowledge of hidden things in the counsel and in 31:23 lead into this account of the reach of divine knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r7.anchor: تكرر فيما سبق من هذه السورة وصف الله تعالى بإحاطة العلم بجميع الأشياء ظاهرة وخفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r8.claim: God reveals some knowledge to chosen messengers when wisdom requires it and keeps other knowledge to Himself when wisdom requires withholding it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r8.anchor: بإثبات أن لعلم الله تعالى مظاهر يبلغ بعضها إلى من اصطفاه من رسله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r9.claim: If God chose to communicate all that He knows, even creatures fit to record His words could not contain it, much less could oral transmission suffice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r9.anchor: وأنه لو شاء أن يبلغ ما في علمه لما وفت به مخلوقاته الصالحة لتسجيل كلامه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r10.claim: The stories of Luqman here and the People of the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn in al-Kahf prepare for that surah’s parallel image of the sea as ink, closely resembling this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r10.anchor: فعقبتا بقوله في آخر السورة : { قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r1.speaker: أصحاب التأويل من السلف من أصحاب ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r1.claim: Early interpreters associated with Ibn ‘Abbās explain the otherwise obscure placement of this verse in its context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r1.anchor: أخذ أصحاب التأويل من السلف من أصحاب ابن عباس في بيان إيقاع هذه الآية في هذا الموقع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن يسار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r2.claim: Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr, ‘Ikrima, and ‘Aṭā’ ibn Yasār report with near variants that Jews questioned the Prophet, or prompted Quraysh to question him, after 17:85; they objected that the Torah explains everything. He replied that it is little beside God’s knowledge, then these verses were revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن يسار بروايات متقاربة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r3.claim: Al-Suddī reports that Quraysh complained that Muhammad spoke too much, and these verses were revealed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r4.claim: Qatāda reports Quraysh said Muhammad’s speech would end or run out, and the verse was revealed; another narration phrases it as ‘this speech will run out.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r4.anchor: سيتم هذا الكلام لمحمد وينحسر أي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا يقول بعده كلاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r5.claim: Some reports imply a Medinan revelation, requiring prophetic direction to place the verse here for its thematic fit; others imply a Meccan revelation inserted after earlier verses as Luqman was revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r5.anchor: وهذه يرجع بعضها إلى أن هذه الآية نزلت بالمدينة فيلزم أن يكون وضعها في هذا الموضع من السورة بتوقيف نبوي للمناسبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r6.claim: كلمات is a plural meaning speech: God’s utterances to angels and other creatures, His creative command Be, and revelation to prophets from the earliest times through Muhammad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r6.anchor: و { كلمات } جمع كلمة بمعنى الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r7.claim: Even if every tree became writing pens and the sea and added seas supplied ink, all the pens and ink would be exhausted while God’s words remained inexhaustible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p181/r7.anchor: أن يكتب كلامه كله صحفا ففرضت الأشجار كلها مقسمة أقلاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r1.claim: The completion of God’s words in 6:115 means their fulfillment and effectiveness; al-Anfāl likewise speaks of God establishing truth by His words.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r2.claim: The concise, artful argument begins with لو to mark its content as a hypothetical; the author refers to Sībawayh’s usage as discussed in Mughnī al-Labīb and to another Quranic example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r2.anchor: وقد نظمت هذه الآية بإيجاز بديع إذ ابتدئت بحرف لو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r3.claim: من شجرة explains the relative ما as a specification and therefore remains singular rather than أشجار.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r3.anchor: بيان ل { ما } الموصولة وهو في معنى التمييز فحقه الإفراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r4.claim: A قلم is a split reed for holding ink and writing; each tree is imagined as supplying as many pens as it has suitable branches, and the plural can denote few or many.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r5.claim: With an open ياء and ḍamma on ميم, يمده means to increase the sea’s ink; it presumes the sea is ink and more seas replenish it as it dries, a concise sense lost with أمده.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r6.claim: Seven often stands idiomatically for a great number, as in the Prophet’s saying that an unbeliever eats in seven intestines; the number is not restrictive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r6.anchor: تستعمل في الكناية عن الكثرة كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r7.claim: ما نفدت means God’s words do not end; this refutes Jews who treat the Torah as the limit of His words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r7.anchor: ومعنى { ما نفدت كلمات الله } ما انتهت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r8.claim: The same image can answer polytheists who think the Quran’s revelation is nearly finished; on this reading, God’s words mean the Quran and exaggerate how much more will be revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r8.anchor: أو كيف يحسب المشركون أن ما نزل من القرآن أوشك أن يكون انتهاء القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r9.claim: The closing clause is a summation: God’s might defeats those awaiting the Prophet’s embarrassment, and His wisdom has no end, so neither do His words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p182/r9.anchor: فهو لعزته لا يغلبه الذين يزعمون عدم الحاجة إلى القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r1.claim: Most readers put البحر in the nominative as a circumstantial nominal clause describing the trees while the sea is their ink; the circumstantial waw links the simultaneous state without a pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r1.anchor: على أن الجملة الاسمية في موضع الحال والواو واو الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r2.claim: Abū ‘Amr and Ya‘qūb read البحر in the accusative, coordinating it with the noun of إن.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p183/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب { والبحر } بالنصب عطفا على اسم ( إن )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r1.claim: Qatada says the sūra is Meccan except two verses, beginning at verse 27.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r1.anchor: قال قتادة أولهما: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says three verses are exceptions, the first beginning at verse 27.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p345/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ثلاث آيات أولهن ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews challenged limited knowledge because the Torah contains God’s speech and rulings; Muhammad replied that the Torah is little of much.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أن سبب هذه الآية أن اليهود قالت يا محمد كيف عنينا بهذا القول وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the Jewish question the correct occasion and says the verse is Medinan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r2.anchor: وهذا هو القول الصحيح، والآية مدنية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r3.claim: Some say Quraysh predicted Muhammad’s speech would run out and he would be cut off.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: سبب الآية أن قريشا قالت سيتم هذا الكلام لمحمد وينجسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Quraysh remarked on how abundant Muhammad’s speech was.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: قالت قريش ما أكثر كلام محمد فنزلت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r5.claim: God’s words are intrinsically unlimited; finite trees and seas make the idea imaginable through the greatest abundance humans know.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r5.anchor: والغرض منها الإعلام بكثرة كلمات الله تعالى وهي في نفسها غير متناهية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r6.claim: The verse says the words would not be exhausted by the stated pens and seas; it does not imply that adding more would exhaust them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r7.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r7.claim: Abu Ali takes God’s words to mean what remains in the realm of decree, not what has come into existence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: المراد ب «الكلمات» والله أعلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r8.claim: Another group understands God’s words as referring to all things known to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r8.anchor: وذهبت فرقة إلى أن «الكلمات» هنا إشارة إلى المعلومات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya notes that this understanding tends toward Muʿtazilism because they regard divine speech as created.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r9.anchor: وهذا قول ينحو إلى الاعتزال من حيث يرون في الكلام أنه مخلوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r10.claim: These readers pronounce al-baḥr in the accusative, coordinating it with the noun of anna.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده من السبعة وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى «والبحر» بالنصب عطفا على «ما»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r11.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r11.claim: The majority read al-baḥr in the nominative as a subject, with the following clause as its predicate; Sibawayh estimates “its state is thus.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r11.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس و «البحر» بالرفع على أنه ابتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r12.speaker: بعض النحويين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r12.claim: Some grammarians coordinate al-baḥr with anna, which occupies a nominative position as a subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r12.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين هو عطف على «أن» لأنها في موضع رفع بالابتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r13.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r13.claim: The majority read yamudduhu from the verb madda.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r14.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r14.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan reads yamudduhu from amadda.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r14.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «يمده» من أمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r15.claim: One group says madda and amadda have the same meaning.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r16.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r16.claim: Another group says madda extends something from itself, while amadda supplies something external; the seven seas are separate from the present sea.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r16.anchor: وقالت فرقة مد الشيء بعضه بعضا وأمد الشيء ما ليس منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r17.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r17.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad reads al-baḥr madāduhu, using the verbal noun madād.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r17.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد «والبحر مداده» وهو مصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “and a sea that it replenishes.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r19.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#4/r19.claim: Al-Hasan reads “God’s speech” in the singular.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p354/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p354/r1.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p354/r1.claim: Al-Naqqash relates that Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abu al-Aswad, and Nabih and Munabbih sons of al-Hajjaj questioned gradual childhood growth versus resurrection all at once.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p354/r1.anchor: وحكى النقاش أن هذه الآية في أبي بن خلف وأبي الأسود ونبيه ومنبه ابني الحجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi points to earlier explanations of the surrounding wording in Hud, al-Ankabut, and al-Baqara.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r1.anchor: وما بعد هذا قد تقدم تفسير ألفاظه في مواضع هود 48 العنكبوت 61 البقرة 267

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, says Jewish scholars asked whether the statement that people received little knowledge referred to them or Muhammad's people; after they cited the Torah's comprehensive knowledge, the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r2.anchor: أن أحبار اليهود قالوا لرسول الله ( ص ) أرأيت قول الله عز وجل وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r3.claim: Qatada says the polytheists claimed the Quran was speech that would soon be exhausted, prompting this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r3.anchor: والثاني أن المشركين قالوا في القرآن إنما هو كلام يوشك أن ينفد وينقطع فنزلت هذه الآية قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r4.claim: If every earthly tree were made into pens and the sea plus seven more seas into ink, the pens and seas would run out before God's words did; the omitted phrase is that they write His words.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r4.anchor: ومعنى الآية لو كانت شجر الأرض أقلاما وكان البحر ومعه سبعة أبحر مدادا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r5.claim: These readers recite al-baḥru in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r5.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي والبحر بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r6.claim: Abu Amr recites al-baḥra in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r6.anchor: ونصبه أبو عمرو وقال الزجاج من قرأ والبحر بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the accusative coordinates with mā, understood as if the verse said if all things on earth and the sea were pens and ink.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r7.anchor: من قرأ والبحر بالنصب فهو عطف على ما المعنى ولو أن ما في الأرض ولو أن البحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the nominative also works by treating the sea as a new clause describing its present state.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r8.anchor: والرفع حسن على معنى والبحر هذه حاله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r9.speaker: اليزيدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r9.claim: Al-Yazidi takes yمده to mean that the sea is increased, as when one says to add water to a pot.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r9.anchor: قال اليزيدي ومعنى يمده من بعده يزيد فيه يقال مد قدرك أي زد في مائها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
