IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the word from ink (midād), not from assistance or reinforcement (imdād), citing ink supplied to an inkwell versus money and men supplied to someone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p325#3/r10.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن قتيبة يمده من المداد لا من الإمداد يقال مددت دواتي بالمداد وأمددته بالمال والرجال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r1.claim: God’s grandeur, sublime names and attributes, and perfect words cannot be encompassed; the Prophet says he cannot enumerate praise as God praises Himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r1.anchor: كما قال سيد البشر وخاتم الرسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r2.claim: If all trees became pens and the sea, joined by seven more seas, became ink to write of God’s majesty, pens would break and water run out, even with more supplies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r2.anchor: أي: ولو أن جميع أشجار الأرض جعلت أقلاما، وجعل البحر مدادا ومده سبعة أبحر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r3.claim: Seven is rhetorical intensification, not a limit or a claim that seven seas surround the world; that literal claim comes from Israelite material neither confirmed nor denied.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r3.anchor: على وجه المبالغة، ولم يرد الحصر ولا [أن] (3) ثم سبعة أبحر موجودة تحيط بالعالم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r4.claim: Quran 18:109 similarly says the sea would run out before God’s words; ‘another like it’ means repeated further supplies without limit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r4.anchor: بل كما قال تعالى في الآية الأخرى: {قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says that if trees were pens and seas ink, God’s decrees would exhaust the seas and break the pens.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: لو جعل شجر الأرض أقلاما، وجعل البحر مدادا، وقال الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r6.claim: Qatada says polytheists claimed this speech would soon run out; the verse answers that God’s wonders, wisdom, creation, and knowledge would not be exhausted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: قال المشركون: إنما هذا كلام يوشك أن ينفد، فقال الله تعالى: {ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas compares all human knowledge with God’s knowledge to a drop of water beside all the seas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: إن مثل علم العباد كلهم في علم الله كقطرة من ماء البحور كلها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r8.claim: Even if every tree were a pen and every sea ink, pens and water would run out while God’s words remain; no one can fully measure or praise Him except by His own praise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348#2/r8.anchor: لانكسرت الأقلام، وفني ماء البحر، وبقيت كلمات الله قائمة لا يفنيها شيء؛ لأن أحدا لا يستطيع أن يقدر قدره،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jewish scholars in Medina asked whether the warning that people received little knowledge referred to them or Muhammad’s people; the Prophet said no, and explained their Torah knowledge was little beside God’s but enough for them. The verse was revealed in response.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أو عكرمة، عن ابن عباس؛ أن أحبار يهود قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة: يا محمد، أرأيت قولك:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r2.claim: Reports from Ikrima and Ata ibn Yasar also make the occasion Medinan, but the better-known view is that the sura and verse are Meccan; Ibn Kathir says God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349/r2.anchor: وهكذا روي عن عكرمة، وعطاء بن يسار. وهذا يقتضي أن هذه الآية مدنية لا مكية، والمشهور أنها مكية،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349#2/r1.claim: Al-Aziz means God has subdued everything, with no one able to prevent His will or overturn His judgment; al-Hakim describes His wisdom in creation, commands, speech, deeds, law, and all affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p349#2/r1.anchor: أي: عزيز قد عز كل شيء وقهره وغلبه، فلا مانع لما أراد ولا مخالف ولا معقب لحكمه، {حكيم} في خلقه وأمره،

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r2.claim: The other readers use nominative al-baḥru, either as a new clause or coordinated with the raised position of anna after law.
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالرفع، وفيه وجهان: أولهما: أنه ابتداء، وثانيهما: معطوفا على محل (أن)

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r7.claim: Madd means extension; a sea is extended when another body of water flows into it continuously, as in tides and tributaries.
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r7.anchor: المد: مد الشيء، ومد البحر: جري غيره إليه حالا بعد حال، ومنه: المد والجزر

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r11.claim: One occasion says the verse answered Jews who claimed Muḥammad’s recited words would run out and break off, and who were waiting for that to happen.
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r11.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (ولو أنما في الأرض) الآية، جوابا لليهود لما قالوا: هذا الكلام الذي يتلوه محمد سينفد وينقطع

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews said they had been given the Torah containing all wisdom, prompting the revelation.
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: بل قالت اليهود: أوتينا التوراة وفيها كل حكمة، فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r13.claim: Another occasion says the Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit; after the reply that they had little knowledge, they countered that they had the Torah in its abundance, and this verse followed.
JISHUMI:v8p5661#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: سألوا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الروح، فنزلت (وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.claim: والبحر is read in the accusative, coordinated with إن’s noun, or in the nominative, coordinated with its syntactic position; the nominative may instead begin a clause with circumstantial wāw.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.anchor: قرىء : ( والبحر ) بالنصب عطفا على اسم إن ، وبالرفع عطفا على محل إن ، ومعمولها على

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads بحر يمده with the noun indefinite; al-Zamakhsharī says it must be explained by the first grammatical analysis.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : و ( بحر يمده ) على التنكير ، ويجب أن يحمل هذا على الوجه الأول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.claim: The verb is also read with the cited variants in form and with either tāʾ or yāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.anchor: وقرىء : ( يمده ) و ( يمده ) وبالتاء والياء .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.claim: Though one might expect the sea to be called ink, يمده evokes filling an inkpot: the great sea is the pot and seven other seas continually pour in ink.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.anchor: أغنى عن ذكر المداد قوله : يمده ، لأنه من قولك : مد الدواة وأمدها ، جعل البحر الأعظم بمنزلة الدواة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.claim: Even if earth’s trees became pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, became ink, writing God’s words would exhaust pen and ink without exhausting His words, as 18:109 says.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.anchor: ولو أن أشجار الأرض أقلام ، والبحر ممدود بسبعة أبحر . وكتبت بتلك الأقلام وبذلك المداد كلمات الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.claim: The circumstantial clause البحر يمده has no explicit pronoun returning to the possessor of the state, like the cited examples; such circumstantials can function like adverbs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.anchor: ليس فيه ضمير راجع إلى ذي الحال . قلت : هو كقوله : وقد اغتدى والطير في وكناتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.claim: Another explanation supplies an omitted possessive pronoun: the sea means the earth’s sea.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : وبحرها ، والضمير للأرض .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r11.claim: The singular شجرة details the trees one by one, so that not a single tree of the kind is left out of the image.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r11.anchor: أريد تفصيل الشجر وتقصيها شجرة شجرة ، حتى لا يبقى من جنس الشجر ولا واحدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r12.claim: Though كلمات is a plural of paucity, it indicates that even seas cannot supply enough to write God’s words, much less His fuller speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r12.anchor: قلت : معناه أن كلماته لا تفي بكتبتها البحار ، فكيف بكلمه ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed in response to Jews who claimed the Torah contained all wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أنها نزلت جوابا لليهود لما قالوا : ( قد أوتينا التوراة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r14.claim: Another account says polytheists claimed the revelation would run out, and God answered that His speech does not run out.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : إن المشركين قالوا : إن هذا يعنون الوحي كلام سينفد ، فأعلم الله أن كلامه لا ينفد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r15.claim: Some classify the verse as Medinan and revealed after the Hijra; another account says it is Meccan and the Jews prompted Quraysh’s delegation to ask about the Torah’s claim to all knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r15.anchor: وهذه الآية عند بعضهم مدنية ، وأنها نزلت بعد الهجرة ، وقيل هي مكية ، وإنما أمر اليهود وفد قريش

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r16.claim: God’s might means nothing can thwart Him, and His wisdom means nothing falls outside His knowledge and ordering; therefore His words and decrees cannot be exhausted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r16.anchor: { أن الله عزيز } لا يعجزه شيء { حكيم } لا يخرج من علمه وحكمته شيء ، ومثله لا تنفد كلماته وحكمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r1.claim: Qatada says the polytheists claimed Quranic speech would soon run out; the verse answers that trees made into pens and seas used as ink would be exhausted before God's marvels, wisdom, and knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r1.anchor: ما رواه سعيد عن قتادة أن المشركين قالوا إنما هو كلام يعني القرآن يوشك أن ينفد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Jewish scholars in Medina asked whether the statement that people received little knowledge referred to them or the Arabs; the Prophet said it referred to all, and they objected that the Torah explains everything. He replied that this is little relative to God's knowledge, and the verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r2.anchor: رواه ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قدم المدينة قالت له أحبار اليهود يا محمد أرأيت قولك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r3.claim: Madda means to add something gradually; the text contrasts it with amadda, used for providing assistance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r3.anchor: أي يزيد فيه شيئا بعد شيء فيقال في الزيادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r4.claim: Nafida describes a thing whose end comes after its beginning is exhausted; one does not use it for something that perishes all at once.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r4.anchor: ونفاد الشيء هو فناء آخره بعد نفاد أوله فلا يقال لما فني جملة : نفد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r5.claim: One interpretation of God's words is His favors to the obedient in Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r5.anchor: أحدها : أنها نعم الله على أهل طاعته في الجنة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r6.claim: Another interpretation is the different kinds of God's creatures.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r7.claim: A third interpretation is everything God decreed for His creatures in the Preserved Tablet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r7.anchor: الثالث : جميع ما قضاه في اللوح المحفوظ من أمور خلقه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p344/r8.claim: A fourth interpretation is God's knowledge.

MUQATIL:31:27-28/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:27-28/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:27-28/r1.claim: If every tree became pens and seven seas supplied ink for all creation to record God’s knowledge and wonders, the pens and seas would run out while His knowledge, words, and wonders would not.
MUQATIL:31:27-28/r1.anchor: يعنى علم الله يقول: لو أن كل شجرة ذات ساق على وجه الأرض بريت أقلاما

MUQATIL:31:27-28/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:27-28/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:27-28/r2.claim: God is mighty in His kingdom and wise in His command; no one can comprehend His knowledge.
MUQATIL:31:27-28/r2.anchor: فى أمره، يخبر الناس أن أحدا لا يدرك علمه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r1.claim: The polytheists claimed revelation would run out; God answers that His words cannot be exhausted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r1.anchor: قال المشركون ان هذا أى الوحى كلام سينفد فأعلم الله أن كلامه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r2.claim: Even if every earthly tree became pens and the ocean, supplied by seven more seas, became ink, God's words would not run out; compare 18:109.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r2.anchor: ولو أن اشجار الأرض أقلام والبحر ممدودا بسبعة أبحر وكتبت بتلك الاقلام وبذلك المداد كلمات الله لما نفدت كلماته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r3.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read al-baḥr in the accusative, coordinated with mā after inna; the nominative can follow the syntactic position of inna and its clause or make al-baḥr an initial clause with a circumstantial wāw.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r3.anchor: والبحر بالنصب أبو عمرو ويعقوب عطفا على اسم أن وهو ما والرفع على محل أن ومعمولها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r4.claim: An alternate reading of yمده is also reported.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r5.claim: Rather than say 'the sea is ink,' the verse says it is supplied: the great sea is like an inkwell continually filled by seven seas that never run dry.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r5.anchor: وكان مقتضى الكلام أن يقال ولو ان الشجر أقلام والبحر مداد لكن أعنى عن ذكر المداد قوله يمده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r6.claim: Shajara is singular to describe the trees one by one, until not a single tree remains unshaved into pens.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r6.anchor: وانما ذكر شجرة على التوحيد لأنه أريد تفصيل الشجر وتقصيها شجرة شجرة حتى لا يبقى من جنس الشجر ولا واحدة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r7.claim: The plural of paucity kalimāt is preferred over the plural of abundance kalim to stress that even the seas cannot suffice to write God's words, let alone one word.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r7.anchor: وأوثر الكلمات وهى جمع قلة على الكلم وهى جمع كثيرة لأن معناه ان كلماته لا تفى بكتبتها البحار فكيف بكلمة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r8.claim: ʿAzīz means that nothing can overpower God.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r9.claim: Ḥakīm means nothing falls outside God's knowledge and wisdom.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#7/r9.anchor: لا يخرج من علمه وحكمته شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r1.claim: After arguing against the polytheists, the verse shows that the meanings of God’s words have no end.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r1.anchor: لما احتج على المشركين بما احتج بين أن معاني كلامه سبحانه لا تنفد، وأنها لا نهاية لها.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r2.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r2.claim: Al-Qaffāl says that even trees made into pens and seas used as ink to record creation’s wonders, proving God’s power and unity, could not exhaust them.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r2.anchor: وقال القفال: لما ذكر أنه سخر لهم ما في السموات وما في الأرض وأنه أسبغ النعم نبه على أن الأشجار لو كانت أقلاما

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r3.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r3.claim: Al-Qushayrī reads the words as divine capacities, but says eternal speech is the stronger reading: created things are finite, future divine creations are unending, and the eternal has no end.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r3.anchor: قال القشيري: فرد معنى تلك الكلمات إلى المقدورات، وحمل الآية على الكلام القديم أولى والمخلوق لا بد له من نهاية،

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r4.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the words denote what remains within God’s power, not what has already come into existence; their many meanings are unbounded, while pens and seas merely illustrate abundance to human understanding.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r4.anchor: وقال أبو علي: المراد بالكلمات والله أعلم ما في المقدور دون ما خرج منه إلى الوجود.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r5.claim: The author says the verse’s context indicates that the words mean God’s eternal speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r5.anchor: ومعنى نزول الآية: يدل على أن المراد بالكلمات الكلام القديم.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews challenged Muḥammad with 17:85, citing the Torah’s speech and rulings against his claim that his Book explains everything; the Prophet replied that the Torah is little of much, and this Medinan verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن سبب هذه الآية أن اليهود قالت: يا محمد، كيف عنينا بهذا القول

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās explains the words as God’s knowledge and the realities of things, including every created kind, part, quality, and change; even seven added seas could not contain their full written account.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر النحاس: فقد تبين أن الكلمات هاهنا يراد بها العلم وحقائق الأشياء لأنه عز وجل علم قبل أن يخلق الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r8.claim: The author calls al-Naḥḥās’s detailed account a good explanation of al-Qaffāl’s view of the abundant meanings and realities signified by God’s words.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27/r8.anchor: قلت: هذا معنى قول القفال، وهو قول حسن إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r1.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r1.claim: One report says Quraysh predicted Muḥammad’s speech would be completed and exhausted, prompting the verse’s revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r1.anchor: وقال قوم: إن قريشا قالت سيتم هذا الكلام لمحمد وينحسر فنزلت.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Quraysh complained that Muḥammad spoke too much, and the verse was revealed in response.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: قالت قريش ما أكثر كلام محمد! فنزلت.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r3.claim: The majority read al-baḥru nominative as a subject whose predicate is the following clause; the full clause is circumstantial, as Sībawayh parsed it.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r3.anchor: قراءة الجمهور بالرفع على الابتداء، وخبره في الجملة التي بعدها، والجملة في موضع الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r4.speaker: بعض النحويين
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r4.claim: Some grammarians parse the nominative al-baḥru as coordinated with anna’s subject because anna is itself in the position of a nominative subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: هو عطف على «أن» لأنها في موضع رفع بالابتداء.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Isḥāq read al-baḥra in the accusative, coordinated with mā, the subject of anna.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن إسحاق: «والبحر» بالنصب على العطف على «ما» وهي اسم «أن».

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r6.speaker: ابن هرمز والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r6.claim: Ibn Hurmuz and al-Ḥasan read yamudduhu from amadda.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز والحسن: «يمده» من أمد.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r7.claim: One group says madd and amadd are synonymous.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r8.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r8.claim: Another group distinguishes them: madd extends something from itself, while amadd supplies what is external to it; the Nile adding to a gulf illustrates madd.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة: مد الشيء بعضه بعضا كما تقول: مد النيل الخليج أي زاد فيه. وأمد الشيء ما ليس منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r9.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r9.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad reads al-baḥru madāduhu, the sea as its ink.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r10.claim: The author refers to earlier discussion of this wording in al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r10.anchor: وقد مضى هذا في «البقرة. وآل عمران».

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r11.claim: The author says the meaning of God’s words was discussed earlier at the end of al-Kahf.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r12.claim: The closing description as Mighty and Wise was also discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r12.anchor: { إن الله عزيز حكيم } تقدم أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the sea here is fresh water, which grows the trees used for pens; salt water does not grow them.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:27#2/r13.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: البحر هاهنا الماء العذب الذي ينبت الأقلام، وأما الماء الملح فلا ينبت الأقلام.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r3.claim: The universe contains such abundant signs of God’s power and wisdom that even all trees as pens and all seas plus seven more as ink could not record them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r3.anchor: if all the trees become pens and all the seas together with seven more become ink, it is still not possible to note down all these signs.
